Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>
c_deckLoaded: boolean = false
c_cardIndex: number = 0
c_flipped: boolean = false
c_knownCount: number = 0
c_missedCount: number = 0
c_deckDone: boolean = false
c_search: string = ""
</fields>
<functions>
function c_deckTerm(i: number): string {
  if (i === 0) { return "tachycardia"; }
  if (i === 1) { return "dyspnea"; }
  if (i === 2) { return "edema"; }
  if (i === 3) { return "cyanosis"; }
  if (i === 4) { return "myocardial infarction"; }
  if (i === 5) { return "hyperglycemia"; }
  if (i === 6) { return "hypoxia"; }
  return "auscultation";
}

function c_deckDefinition(i: number): string {
  if (i === 0) { return "heart rate above 100 bpm"; }
  if (i === 1) { return "difficult or labored breathing"; }
  if (i === 2) { return "swelling from fluid in tissues"; }
  if (i === 3) { return "bluish skin from low oxygen"; }
  if (i === 4) { return "death of heart muscle from blocked blood flow"; }
  if (i === 5) { return "high blood sugar"; }
  if (i === 6) { return "low oxygen in tissues"; }
  return "listening to body sounds with a stethoscope";
}

function c_loadDeck(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { out.push(e); }
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < 8) {
    let term: string = c_deckTerm(i);
    let found: boolean = false;
    for (let e: LogEntry of out) {
      if (e.term === term) { found = true; }
    }
    if (!found) {
      out.push({term: term, definition: c_deckDefinition(i), timesMissed: 0, minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()});
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return {entries: out, c_deckLoaded: true, c_cardIndex: 0, c_flipped: false, c_knownCount: 0, c_missedCount: 0, c_deckDone: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_flip(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_flipped: !state.c_flipped__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_markKnown(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let next: number = state.c_cardIndex + 1;
  let done: boolean = next >= 8;
  return {c_cardIndex: next, c_flipped: false, c_knownCount: state.c_knownCount + 1, c_deckDone: done__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_markMissed(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let term: string = c_deckTerm(state.c_cardIndex);
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    let e: LogEntry = state.entries[i];
    if (e.term === term) {
      out.push({term: e.term, definition: e.definition, timesMissed: e.timesMissed + 1, minute: e.minute});
    } else {
      out.push(e);
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let next: number = state.c_cardIndex + 1;
  let done: boolean = next >= 8;
  return {entries: out, c_cardIndex: next, c_flipped: false, c_missedCount: state.c_missedCount + 1, c_deckDone: done__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_restartDeck(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_cardIndex: 0, c_flipped: false, c_knownCount: 0, c_missedCount: 0, c_deckDone: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setSearch(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_search: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  if (!state.c_deckLoaded) {
    sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [
      ui.Text("body", "Load the starter deck of eight medical term flashcards to begin flipping through them."),
      ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Load starter deck", "c_loadDeck", 0, true)])
    ]));
  } else {
    if (state.c_deckDone) {
      sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "", "", [
        ui.SectionHeader("default", "Deck complete", "", ""),
        ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
          ui.NumberStat("success", "Known", state.c_knownCount, "", "", 1, "", "check"),
          ui.NumberStat("danger", "Missed", state.c_missedCount, "", "", 1, "added to your list", "warning")
        ]),
        ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Go through again", "c_restartDeck", 0, true)])
      ]));
    } else {
      let front: string = c_deckTerm(state.c_cardIndex);
      let back: string = c_deckDefinition(state.c_cardIndex);
      let shown: string = front;
      if (state.c_flipped) { shown = back; }
      let side: string = "TERM";
      if (state.c_flipped) { side = "DEFINITION"; }
      let cardChildren: ui.View[] = [];
      cardChildren.push(ui.Text("eyebrow", side));
      cardChildren.push(ui.Text("title", shown));
      cardChildren.push(ui.Text("caption", "Card " + ui.numberToString(state.c_cardIndex + 1) + " of 8"));
      sections.push(ui.Section("hero", "", "", [
        ui.Card("surface", cardChildren),
        ui.ActionBar("spread", [
          ui.Button("secondary", "Flip", "c_flip", 0, true),
          ui.Button("success", "Known", "c_markKnown", 0, state.c_flipped),
          ui.Button("danger", "Missed", "c_markMissed", 0, state.c_flipped)
        ])
      ]));
    }
    let query: string = strings.toLowerCase(strings.trim(state.c_search));
    let matches: number = 0;
    let i: number = 0;
    while (i < state.entries.length()) {
      let e: LogEntry = state.entries[i];
      let hay: string = strings.toLowerCase(e.term + " " + e.definition);
      if (query === "" || strings.contains(hay, query)) { matches = matches + 1; }
      i = i + 1;
    }
    let searchChildren: ui.View[] = [];
    searchChildren.push(ui.TextField("default", "Search missed terms", state.c_search, "c_setSearch"));
    if (query !== "") {
      searchChildren.push(ui.Text("caption", ui.numberToString(matches) + " of " + ui.numberToString(state.entries.length()) + " terms match"));
    }
    sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", searchChildren));
  }
}
</view>

- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.

Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.

}

function c_markMissed(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {

    } else {
      out.push(e);
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let next: number = state.c_cardIndex + 1;
  let done: boolean = next >= 8;
  return {entries: out, c_cardIndex: next, c_flipped: false, c_missedCount: state.c_missedCount + 1, c_deckDone: done__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_restartDeck(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_cardIndex: 0, c_flipped: false, c_knownCount: 0, c_missedCount: 0, c_deckDone: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_startEdit(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  let current: string = "0";
  if (value >= 0 && value < state.entries.length()) {
    current = ui.formatNumber(state.entries[value].timesMissed, 0);
  }
  return {c_editIndex: value, c_editValue: current__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setEditValue(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_editValue: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_saveEdit(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_editIndex < 0 || state.c_editIndex >= state.entries.length()) {
    return {c_editIndex: -1, c_editValue: ""__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let parsed: number = strings.toNumber(strings.trim(state.c_editValue), -1);
  if (parsed < 0) {
    return {c_editIndex: -1, c_editValue: ""__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let whole: number = math.floor(parsed);
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    let e: LogEntry = state.entries[i];
    if (i === state.c_editIndex) {
      out.push({term: e.term, definition: e.definition, timesMissed: whole, minute: e.minute});
    } else {
      out.push(e);
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return {entries: out, c_editIndex: -1, c_editValue: ""__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>

</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.

function c_orderOf(state: AppState): number[] {

function c_priorCredits(state: AppState): number {

function c_entryCredits(state: AppState): number {

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>

</fields>
<functions>
function c_priorCredits(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = strings.toNumber(state.priorCreditsText, 0);
  if (n < 0) { return 0; }
  return n;
}

function c_priorGpa(state: AppState): number {
  let g: number = strings.toNumber(state.priorGpa, 0);
  if (g < 0) { return 0; }
  if (g > 4) { return 4; }
  return g;
}

function c_entryCredits(state: AppState): number {
  let total: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.termCredits > 0) { total = total + e.termCredits; }
  }
  return total;
}

function c_totalCredits(state: AppState): number {
  return c_priorCredits(state) + c_entryCredits(state);
}

function c_cumulativeGpa(state: AppState): number {
  let credits: number = c_totalCredits(state);
  if (credits <= 0) { return 0; }
  let points: number = c_priorGpa(state) * c_priorCredits(state);
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.termCredits > 0) { points = points + e.termGpa * e.termCredits; }
  }
  return points / credits;
}

function c_clearAll(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  return {entries: none, removedEntries: none, removedAt: -1__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let c_credits: number = c_totalCredits(state);
  let c_gpa: number = c_cumulativeGpa(state);
  let c_hasTerms: boolean = state.entries.length() > 0;
  let c_hasPrior: boolean = c_priorCredits(state) > 0;
  let c_ready: boolean = c_hasTerms || c_hasPrior;
  let c_stats: ui.View[] = [];
  c_stats.push(ui.NumberStat("default", "Total credits", c_credits, "", "", 1, "before plus every term", "list"));
  c_stats.push(ui.NumberStat("accent", "Cumulative GPA", c_gpa, "", "", 1, "credit-weighted", "star"));
  let c_actions: ui.View[] = [];
  c_actions.push(ui.Button("danger", "Clear all terms", "c_clearAll", 0, c_hasTerms));
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "Cumulative", "Across every term and your prior record", [
    ui.When(c_ready, ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, c_stats)),
    ui.When(!c_ready, ui.Text("muted", "Your total credits and cumulative GPA appear here once you set credits before or add a term.")),
    ui.When(c_hasTerms, ui.ActionBar("end", c_actions))
  ]));
}
</view>

  if (kept <= 0) { return 0; }
  return c_keptTotal(state) / kept;
}

function c_clearScores(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {scores: ""__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let keptScores: number = c_keptCount(state);
  let droppedTotal: number = c_droppedTotal(state);
  let keptTotal: number = c_keptTotal(state);
  let finalGrade: number = c_finalGrade(state);
  let totalScores: number = c_parseScores(state.scores).length();
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "Results", "Lowest scores dropped", [
    ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.NumberStat("default", "Kept scores", keptScores, "", "", 1, "of " + ui.numberToString(totalScores), "list"),
      ui.NumberStat("default", "Dropped total", droppedTotal, "", "", 1, "points removed", "minus"),
      ui.NumberStat("default", "Kept total", keptTotal, "", "", 1, "points counted", "plus"),
      ui.NumberStat("accent", "Final grade", finalGrade, "", "%", 1, "average of kept scores", "star")
    ]),
    ui.ActionBar("end", [
      ui.Button("secondary", "Clear scores", "c_clearScores", 0, totalScores > 0)
    ])
  ]));
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

Request: dropped lowest score grade calc

The section must do:
- the figure "Kept scores": the scores left after dropping the lowest ones (the plan works it out as max(0, count(scores) - dropCount); for scores = 5, dropCount = 1 that is 4)
- the figure "Dropped total": the sum of the lowest scores that are dropped (the plan works it out as 0; for its example that is 0)
- the figure "Kept total": the sum of the scores that are kept (the plan works it out as 0; for its example that is 0)
- the figure "Final grade": the average of the kept scores (a percent: show it with the % sign) (the plan works it out as keptScores > 0 ? keptTotal / keptScores : 0; for keptScores = 4, keptTotal = 340 that is 85)

The person sets these on the screen and nothing else uses them yet; the section uses them:
- "Scores": state.scores
- "Drop lowest": state.dropCount

}

function set_dropCount(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {dropCount: value, scores: state.scores, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

}

function c_parseScores(text: string): number[] {
  let out: number[] = [];
  let parts: string[] = strings.split(text, ",");
  for (let p: string of parts) {
    let t: string = strings.trim(p);
    if (strings.length(t) > 0) {
      let n: number = strings.toNumber(t, -1);
      if (n >= 0) {
        out.push(n);
      }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function c_keptCount(state: AppState): number {
  let all: number[] = c_parseScores(state.scores);
  let kept: number = all.length() - state.dropCount;
  if (kept < 0) { kept = 0; }
  return kept;
}

function c_droppedTotal(state: AppState): number {
  let all: number[] = c_parseScores(state.scores);
  let n: number = all.length();
  let drop: number = state.dropCount;
  if (drop > n) { drop = n; }
  let total: number = 0;
  let taken: number = 0;
  while (taken < drop) {
    let bestIndex: number = -1;
    let bestValue: number = 0;
    let i: number = 0;
    while (i < n) {
      let v: number = all[i];
      if (v >= 0 && (bestIndex < 0 || v < bestValue)) {
        bestValue = v;
        bestIndex = i;
      }
      i = i + 1;
    }
    if (bestIndex < 0) {
      taken = drop;
    } else {
      total = total + bestValue;
      all[bestIndex] = -1;
      taken = taken + 1;
    }
  }
  return total;
}

function c_keptTotal(state: AppState): number {
  let all: number[] = c_parseScores(state.scores);
  let sum: number = 0;
  for (let v: number of all) {
    sum = sum + v;
  }
  return sum - c_droppedTotal(state);
}

function c_finalGrade(state: AppState): number {
  let kept: number = c_keptCount(state);
  if (kept <= 0) { return 0; }
  return c_keptTotal(state) / kept;
}

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>

</functions>
<view>

</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_rounds: c_buildRounds(), c_index: 0, c_score: 0, c_played: 0, c_picked: -1, c_trigger: state.c_trigger + 1, c_secondsLeft: 30, c_timerRunning: true, c_timedOut: false__PASSTHROUGH__};

  if (state.c_picked !== -1) {

  }
  if (actions.length() > 0) {
    body.push(ui.ActionBar("end", actions));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", body));
}

function c_answerFor(index: number): string {
  if (index === 0) { return "The Lion King"; }
  if (index === 1) { return "Titanic"; }
  if (index === 2) { return "Spider-Man"; }
  if (index === 3) { return "Jurassic Park"; }

  if (index === 5) { return "Finding Nemo"; }
  if (index === 6) { return "The Wizard of Oz"; }

  if (index === 9) { return "Kung Fu Panda"; }
  return "";
}

  return 10;

function c_normalize(s: string): string {
  let t: string = strings.toLowerCase(strings.trim(s));
  t = strings.replace(t, "the ", "");
  t = strings.replace(t, "-", " ");
  t = strings.replace(t, "  ", " ");
  return strings.trim(t);
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>
c_puzzleIndex: number = 0
c_guess: string = ""
c_feedback: string = ""
c_checked: boolean = false
c_lastCorrect: boolean = false
c_hintShown: boolean = false
</fields>
<functions>
function c_emojiFor(index: number): string {
  if (index === 0) { return "🦁👑"; }
  if (index === 1) { return "🚢🧊💔"; }
  if (index === 2) { return "🕷️🧑🕸️"; }
  if (index === 3) { return "🦖🏞️🧬"; }
  if (index === 4) { return "👻🚫👨"; }
  if (index === 5) { return "🐟🔍🤡"; }
  if (index === 6) { return "🌪️🏠👠"; }
  if (index === 7) { return "🦇🧛🌃"; }
  if (index === 8) { return "🚀🌌👨‍🚀"; }
  if (index === 9) { return "🐼🥋🐍"; }
  return "🎬❓";
}

function c_answerFor(index: number): string {
  if (index === 0) { return "The Lion King"; }
  if (index === 1) { return "Titanic"; }
  if (index === 2) { return "Spider-Man"; }
  if (index === 3) { return "Jurassic Park"; }
  if (index === 4) { return "Ghostbusters"; }
  if (index === 5) { return "Finding Nemo"; }
  if (index === 6) { return "The Wizard of Oz"; }
  if (index === 7) { return "Dracula"; }
  if (index === 8) { return "Interstellar"; }
  if (index === 9) { return "Kung Fu Panda"; }
  return "";
}

function c_puzzleCount(): number {
  return 10;
}

function c_normalize(s: string): string {
  let t: string = strings.toLowerCase(strings.trim(s));
  t = strings.replace(t, "the ", "");
  t = strings.replace(t, "-", " ");
  t = strings.replace(t, "  ", " ");
  return strings.trim(t);
}

function c_firstLetter(index: number): string {
  let answer: string = c_answerFor(index);
  if (strings.length(answer) === 0) { return ""; }
  return strings.toUpperCase(strings.substring(answer, 0, 1));
}

function c_setGuess(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_guess: value, c_feedback: "", c_checked: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_showHint(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_hintShown: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_check(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let answer: string = c_answerFor(state.c_puzzleIndex);
  let ok: boolean = c_normalize(state.c_guess) === c_normalize(answer);
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { out.push(e); }
  out.push({movieTitle: answer, correct: ok, minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()});
  let msg: string = "Not quite — the answer was " + answer + ".";
  if (ok) { msg = "Correct! It was " + answer + "."; }
  return {entries: out, c_checked: true, c_lastCorrect: ok, c_feedback: msg__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_next(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = c_puzzleCount();
  let next: number = state.c_puzzleIndex + 1;
  if (next >= n) { next = 0; }
  return {c_puzzleIndex: next, c_guess: "", c_feedback: "", c_checked: false, c_lastCorrect: false, c_hintShown: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let emoji: string = c_emojiFor(state.c_puzzleIndex);
  let puzzleNo: number = state.c_puzzleIndex + 1;
  let total: number = c_puzzleCount();
  let canCheck: boolean = strings.trim(state.c_guess) !== "" && !state.c_checked;
  let cardChildren: ui.View[] = [];
  cardChildren.push(ui.SectionHeader("default", "Puzzle " + ui.numberToString(puzzleNo) + " of " + ui.numberToString(total), "What film is this?", ""));
  cardChildren.push(ui.Text("display", emoji));
  cardChildren.push(ui.TextField("default", "Your guess", state.c_guess, "c_setGuess"));
  if (state.c_hintShown && !state.c_checked) {
    cardChildren.push(ui.InsetBanner("accent", "Hint", "The answer starts with " + c_firstLetter(state.c_puzzleIndex) + ".", "", "", "info"));
  }
  if (state.c_checked) {
    if (state.c_lastCorrect) {
      cardChildren.push(ui.InsetBanner("success", "Correct", state.c_feedback, "", "", "check"));
    } else {
      cardChildren.push(ui.InsetBanner("warning", "Not quite", state.c_feedback, "", "", "info"));
    }
    cardChildren.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Next puzzle", "c_next", 0, true)]));
  } else {
    let actions: ui.View[] = [];
    if (!state.c_hintShown) {
      actions.push(ui.Button("secondary", "Hint", "c_showHint", 0, true));
    }
    actions.push(ui.Button("primary", "Check guess", "c_check", 0, canCheck));
    cardChildren.push(ui.ActionBar("end", actions));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("hero", "", "", [ui.Card("surface", cardChildren)]));
}
</view>

}

      ui.Button("primary", "New word", "c_start", 0, true),
      ui.Button("secondary", "Shuffle", "c_shuffle", 0, true)
    ])
  ]));
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [
    ui.SectionHeader("default", "Pick a letter", "", ""),
    ui.Grid("compact", 7, cells)
  ]));
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

function c_nextSeed(seed: number): number {
  return (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648;
}

function c_buildQuiz(state: AppState): AppState {
  let total: number = state.rounds;
  let pool: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.c_countries.length()) {
    pool.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let order: number[] = [];
  let oa: number[] = [];
  let ob: number[] = [];
  let oc: number[] = [];
  let od: number[] = [];
  let cor: number[] = [];
  let r: number = 0;
  while (r < total && pool.length() > 0) {
    seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
    let pick: number = seed % pool.length();
    let country: number = pool[pick];
    let rest: number[] = [];
    let j: number = 0;
    while (j < pool.length()) {
      if (j !== pick) { rest.push(pool[j]); }
      j = j + 1;
    }
    pool = rest;
    let wrongs: number[] = [];
    let w: number = 0;
    while (w < 3 && pool.length() > 0) {
      seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
      let wp: number = seed % pool.length();
      wrongs.push(pool[wp]);
      let keep: number[] = [];
      let k: number = 0;
      while (k < pool.length()) {
        if (k !== wp) { keep.push(pool[k]); }
        k = k + 1;
      }
      pool = keep;
      w = w + 1;
    }
    while (wrongs.length() < 3) {
      seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
      let filler: number = seed % state.c_countries.length();
      if (filler !== country) { wrongs.push(filler); }
    }
    seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
    let slot: number = seed % 4;
    let opts: number[] = [];
    let wi: number = 0;
    while (wi < 3) {
      opts.push(wrongs[wi]);
      wi = wi + 1;
    }
    let placed: number[] = [];
    let p: number = 0;
    while (p < 4) {
      if (p === slot) { placed.push(country); }
      else {
        let take: number = 0;
        if (p < slot) { take = p; } else { take = p - 1; }
        placed.push(opts[take]);
      }
      p = p + 1;
    }
    order.push(country);
    oa.push(placed[0]);
    ob.push(placed[1]);
    oc.push(placed[2]);
    od.push(placed[3]);
    cor.push(slot);
    r = r + 1;
  }
  return {c_order: order, c_optionA: oa, c_optionB: ob, c_optionC: oc, c_optionD: od, c_correct: cor, c_round: 0, c_score: 0, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1, c_seed: seed, c_started: true, c_finished: false, c_secondsLeft: state.c_secondsPerQuestion, c_timedOut: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_buildQuiz(state);
}

function c_answer(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_answered || state.c_finished) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let right: number = 0;
  if (state.c_round < state.c_correct.length()) {
    right = state.c_correct[state.c_round];
  }
  let gained: number = 0;
  if (value === right) { gained = state.c_pointsPerCorrect; }
  return {c_answered: true, c_picked: value, c_score: state.c_score + gained, c_timedOut: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_next(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_answered) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let nextRound: number = state.c_round + 1;
  if (nextRound >= state.c_order.length()) {
    return {c_finished: true, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1, c_timedOut: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_round: nextRound, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1, c_secondsLeft: state.c_secondsPerQuestion, c_timedOut: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_restart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_buildQuiz(state);
}

function c_tick(state: AppState, elapsedMs: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_started || state.c_finished || state.c_answered) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let left: number = state.c_secondsLeft - elapsedMs / 1000;
  if (left <= 0) {
    return {c_secondsLeft: 0, c_answered: true, c_picked: -1, c_timedOut: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_secondsLeft: left__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setSeconds(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  let v: number = value;
  if (v < 5) { v = 5; }
  if (v > 60) { v = 60; }
  return {c_secondsPerQuestion: v, c_secondsLeft: v__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

</classes>
<fields>

c_capitals: string[] = ["Paris", "Tokyo", "Brasília", "Nairobi", "Ottawa", "Canberra", "Cairo", "Oslo", "New Delhi", "Mexico City", "Rome", "Bangkok", "Lima", "Athens", "Hanoi", "Rabat", "Madrid", "Ankara", "Santiago", "Warsaw"]

c_optionB: number[] = []
c_optionC: number[] = []
c_optionD: number[] = []
c_correct: number[] = []
c_round: number = 0
c_score: number = 0
c_pointsPerCorrect: number = 1
c_answered: boolean = false
c_picked: number = -1
c_seed: number = 12345
c_started: boolean = false
c_finished: boolean = false
c_streak: number = 0
c_bestStreak: number = 0
</fields>
<functions>
function c_nextSeed(seed: number): number {
  return (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648;
}

function c_buildQuiz(state: AppState): AppState {
  let total: number = state.rounds;
  let pool: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.c_countries.length()) {
    pool.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let order: number[] = [];
  let oa: number[] = [];
  let ob: number[] = [];
  let oc: number[] = [];
  let od: number[] = [];
  let cor: number[] = [];
  let r: number = 0;
  while (r < total && pool.length() > 0) {
    seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
    let pick: number = seed % pool.length();
    let country: number = pool[pick];
    let rest: number[] = [];
    let j: number = 0;
    while (j < pool.length()) {
      if (j !== pick) { rest.push(pool[j]); }
      j = j + 1;
    }
    pool = rest;
    let wrongs: number[] = [];
    let w: number = 0;
    while (w < 3 && pool.length() > 0) {
      seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
      let wp: number = seed % pool.length();
      wrongs.push(pool[wp]);
      let keep: number[] = [];
      let k: number = 0;
      while (k < pool.length()) {
        if (k !== wp) { keep.push(pool[k]); }
        k = k + 1;
      }
      pool = keep;
      w = w + 1;
    }
    while (wrongs.length() < 3) {
      seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
      let filler: number = seed % state.c_countries.length();
      if (filler !== country) { wrongs.push(filler); }
    }
    seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
    let slot: number = seed % 4;
    let opts: number[] = [];
    let wi: number = 0;
    while (wi < 3) {
      opts.push(wrongs[wi]);
      wi = wi + 1;
    }
    let placed: number[] = [];
    let p: number = 0;
    while (p < 4) {
      if (p === slot) { placed.push(country); }
      else {
        let take: number = 0;
        if (p < slot) { take = p; } else { take = p - 1; }
        placed.push(opts[take]);
      }
      p = p + 1;
    }
    order.push(country);
    oa.push(placed[0]);
    ob.push(placed[1]);
    oc.push(placed[2]);
    od.push(placed[3]);
    cor.push(slot);
    r = r + 1;
  }
  return {c_order: order, c_optionA: oa, c_optionB: ob, c_optionC: oc, c_optionD: od, c_correct: cor, c_round: 0, c_score: 0, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1, c_seed: seed, c_started: true, c_finished: false, c_streak: 0, c_bestStreak: 0__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_buildQuiz(state);
}

function c_answer(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_answered || state.c_finished) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let right: number = 0;
  if (state.c_round < state.c_correct.length()) {
    right = state.c_correct[state.c_round];
  }
  let gained: number = 0;
  let streak: number = state.c_streak;
  let best: number = state.c_bestStreak;
  if (value === right) {
    gained = state.c_pointsPerCorrect;
    streak = streak + 1;
    if (streak > best) { best = streak; }
  } else {
    streak = 0;
  }
  return {c_answered: true, c_picked: value, c_score: state.c_score + gained, c_streak: streak, c_bestStreak: best__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_next(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_answered) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let nextRound: number = state.c_round + 1;
  if (nextRound >= state.c_order.length()) {
    return {c_finished: true, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_round: nextRound, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_restart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_buildQuiz(state);
}
</functions>

    labels.push(state.c_capitals[state.c_optionB[current]]);

  }

    ]));

    body.push(ui.ActionBar("center", [ui.Button("primary", "Play again", "c_restart", 0, true)]));
  } else {
    body.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, [
      ui.NumberStat("accent", "Streak", state.c_streak, "", "", 1, "in a row", "star"),

    ]));

    body.push(ui.Hero("accent", "CAPITAL OF", countryName, "Pick the right capital city", []));
