messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>
c_countries: string[] = ["France", "Japan", "Brazil", "Kenya", "Canada", "Australia", "Egypt", "Norway", "India", "Mexico", "Italy", "Thailand", "Peru", "Greece", "Vietnam", "Morocco", "Spain", "Turkey", "Chile", "Poland"]
c_capitals: string[] = ["Paris", "Tokyo", "Brasília", "Nairobi", "Ottawa", "Canberra", "Cairo", "Oslo", "New Delhi", "Mexico City", "Rome", "Bangkok", "Lima", "Athens", "Hanoi", "Rabat", "Madrid", "Ankara", "Santiago", "Warsaw"]
c_order: number[] = []
c_optionA: number[] = []
c_optionB: number[] = []
c_optionC: number[] = []
c_optionD: number[] = []
c_correct: number[] = []
c_round: number = 0
c_score: number = 0
c_pointsPerCorrect: number = 1
c_answered: boolean = false
c_picked: number = -1
c_seed: number = 12345
c_started: boolean = false
c_finished: boolean = false
c_shuffle: boolean = true
</fields>
<functions>
function c_nextSeed(seed: number): number {
  return (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648;
}

function c_buildQuiz(state: AppState): AppState {
  let total: number = state.rounds;
  let pool: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.c_countries.length()) {
    pool.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  if (state.c_shuffle) {
    seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
    let s: number = 0;
    while (s < pool.length()) {
      seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
      let swapAt: number = seed % pool.length();
      let held: number = pool[s];
      pool[s] = pool[swapAt];
      pool[swapAt] = held;
      s = s + 1;
    }
  }
  let order: number[] = [];
  let oa: number[] = [];
  let ob: number[] = [];
  let oc: number[] = [];
  let od: number[] = [];
  let cor: number[] = [];
  let r: number = 0;
  while (r < total && pool.length() > 0) {
    seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
    let pick: number = seed % pool.length();
    let country: number = pool[pick];
    let rest: number[] = [];
    let j: number = 0;
    while (j < pool.length()) {
      if (j !== pick) { rest.push(pool[j]); }
      j = j + 1;
    }
    pool = rest;
    let wrongs: number[] = [];
    let w: number = 0;
    while (w < 3 && pool.length() > 0) {
      seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
      let wp: number = seed % pool.length();
      wrongs.push(pool[wp]);
      let keep: number[] = [];
      let k: number = 0;
      while (k < pool.length()) {
        if (k !== wp) { keep.push(pool[k]); }
        k = k + 1;
      }
      pool = keep;
      w = w + 1;
    }
    while (wrongs.length() < 3) {
      seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
      let filler: number = seed % state.c_countries.length();
      if (filler !== country) { wrongs.push(filler); }
    }
    seed = c_nextSeed(seed);
    let slot: number = seed % 4;
    let opts: number[] = [];
    let wi: number = 0;
    while (wi < 3) {
      opts.push(wrongs[wi]);
      wi = wi + 1;
    }
    let placed: number[] = [];
    let p: number = 0;
    while (p < 4) {
      if (p === slot) { placed.push(country); }
      else {
        let take: number = 0;
        if (p < slot) { take = p; } else { take = p - 1; }
        placed.push(opts[take]);
      }
      p = p + 1;
    }
    order.push(country);
    oa.push(placed[0]);
    ob.push(placed[1]);
    oc.push(placed[2]);
    od.push(placed[3]);
    cor.push(slot);
    r = r + 1;
  }
  return {c_order: order, c_optionA: oa, c_optionB: ob, c_optionC: oc, c_optionD: od, c_correct: cor, c_round: 0, c_score: 0, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1, c_seed: seed, c_started: true, c_finished: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_buildQuiz(state);
}

function c_toggleShuffle(state: AppState, value: boolean): AppState {
  return {c_shuffle: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_answer(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_answered || state.c_finished) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let right: number = 0;
  if (state.c_round < state.c_correct.length()) {
    right = state.c_correct[state.c_round];
  }
  let gained: number = 0;
  if (value === right) { gained = state.c_pointsPerCorrect; }
  return {c_answered: true, c_picked: value, c_score: state.c_score + gained__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_next(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_answered) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let nextRound: number = state.c_round + 1;
  if (nextRound >= state.c_order.length()) {
    return {c_finished: true, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_round: nextRound, c_answered: false, c_picked: -1__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_restart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_buildQuiz(state);
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let total: number = state.c_order.length();
  let current: number = state.c_round;
  let countryName: string = "";
  let correctName: string = "";
  let rightIndex: number = 0;
  if (current < total) {
    countryName = state.c_countries[state.c_order[current]];
    rightIndex = state.c_correct[current];
    if (rightIndex === 0) { correctName = state.c_capitals[state.c_optionA[current]]; }
    if (rightIndex === 1) { correctName = state.c_capitals[state.c_optionB[current]]; }
    if (rightIndex === 2) { correctName = state.c_capitals[state.c_optionC[current]]; }
    if (rightIndex === 3) { correctName = state.c_capitals[state.c_optionD[current]]; }
  }
  let optionViews: ui.View[] = [];
  if (current < total) {
    let labels: string[] = [];
    labels.push(state.c_capitals[state.c_optionA[current]]);
    labels.push(state.c_capitals[state.c_optionB[current]]);
    labels.push(state.c_capitals[state.c_optionC[current]]);
    labels.push(state.c_capitals[state.c_optionD[current]]);
    let oi: number = 0;
    while (oi < 4) {
      let tone: string = "default";
      if (state.c_answered) {
        if (oi === rightIndex) { tone = "success"; }
        else if (oi === state.c_picked) { tone = "danger"; }
      }
      optionViews.push(ui.Cell(tone, labels[oi], "c_answer", oi, !state.c_answered));
      oi = oi + 1;
    }
  }
  let feedback: ui.View[] = [];
  if (state.c_answered) {
    if (state.c_picked === rightIndex) {
      feedback.push(ui.InsetBanner("success", "Correct!", "Nice one.", "", "", "check"));
    } else {
      feedback.push(ui.InsetBanner("danger", "Not quite", "The capital of " + countryName + " is " + correctName + ".", "", "", "close"));
    }
    feedback.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Next round", "c_next", 0, true)]));
  }
  let body: ui.View[] = [];
  if (!state.c_started) {
    body.push(ui.EmptyState("default", "Ready to play?", "Set your rounds above, then start the quiz.", "Start quiz", "c_start", "star"));
  } else if (state.c_finished) {
    body.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.NumberStat("accent", "Score", state.c_score, "", "", 1, "of " + ui.numberToString(total * state.c_pointsPerCorrect), "star"),
      ui.NumberStat("default", "Rounds", total, "", "", 1, "played", "list")
    ]));
    body.push(ui.Progress("accent", "Score", state.c_score, total * state.c_pointsPerCorrect));
    body.push(ui.ActionBar("center", [ui.Button("primary", "Play again", "c_restart", 0, true)]));
  } else {
    body.push(ui.SectionHeader("default", "Round " + ui.numberToString(current + 1) + " of " + ui.numberToString(total), "Score " + ui.numberToString(state.c_score) + " of " + ui.numberToString(total * state.c_pointsPerCorrect), ""));
    body.push(ui.Hero("accent", "CAPITAL OF", countryName, "Pick the right capital city", []));
    body.push(ui.Grid("default", 2, optionViews));
    let fi: number = 0;
    while (fi < feedback.length()) {
      body.push(feedback[fi]);
      fi = fi + 1;
    }
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Quiz", "", body));
  sections.push(ui.Section("supporting", "Game setup", "Each new game can deal the countries in a fresh order", [
    ui.Toggle("default", "Shuffle country order", state.c_shuffle, "c_toggleShuffle")
  ]));
}
</view>

function c_roll(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  let predictionValues: number[] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6];
  let call: number = predictionValues[state.predictionIndex];
  let stake: number = strings.toNumber(state.stakeText, 0);
  if (stake <= 0) {
    return {c_message: "Enter a stake of at least 1 coin."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  if (stake > state.c_coins) {
    return {c_message: "You only have " + ui.numberToString(state.c_coins) + " coins."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let seed: number = time.nowMillis() + state.c_throws * 7919;
  let d1: number = math.randomBelow(seed, 6) + 1;
  let d2: number = math.randomBelow(seed + 31, 6) + 1;
  let won: boolean = d1 === call;
  let delta: number = 0 - stake;
  if (won) { delta = stake; }
  let coinsAfter: number = state.c_coins + delta;
  let entry: C_Roll = {
    die1: d1,
    die2: d2,
    call: call,
    stake: stake,
    won: won,
    coinsAfter: coinsAfter

  let out: C_Roll[] = [];

  let msg: string = "Rolled " + ui.numberToString(d1) + " and " + ui.numberToString(d2) + ". ";

  return {
    c_rolls: out,
    c_coins: coinsAfter,
    c_throws: state.c_throws + 1,
    c_die1: d1,
    c_die2: d2,
    c_hasRolled: true,
    c_message: msg
  __PASSTHROUGH__};

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>

</fields>
<functions>
function c_ln(x: number): number {
  if (x <= 0) { return 0; }
  let y: number = (x - 1) / (x + 1);
  let y2: number = y * y;
  let term: number = y;
  let sum: number = 0;
  let k: number = 0;
  while (k < 40) {
    sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1);
    term = term * y2;
    k = k + 1;
  }
  return 2 * sum;
}

function c_monthsToPayoff(balance: number, monthlyRate: number, payment: number): number {
  if (balance <= 0) { return 0; }
  if (payment <= 0) { return -1; }
  if (monthlyRate <= 0) {
    return math.ceil(balance / payment);
  }
  let ratio: number = (balance * monthlyRate) / payment;
  if (ratio >= 1) { return -1; }
  let denom: number = c_ln(1 + monthlyRate);
  if (denom === 0) { return -1; }
  let raw: number = -c_ln(1 - ratio) / denom;
  return math.ceil(raw);
}

function c_totalInterest(balance: number, monthlyRate: number, payment: number, months: number): number {
  if (months <= 0) { return 0; }
  let remaining: number = balance;
  let paid: number = 0;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < months) {
    let interest: number = remaining * monthlyRate;
    let principal: number = payment - interest;
    if (principal <= 0) { return paid; }
    if (principal > remaining) { principal = remaining; }
    paid = paid + interest;
    remaining = remaining - principal;
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return paid;
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let c_balance: number = strings.toNumber(state.balanceText, 0);
  let c_apr: number = strings.toNumber(state.aprText, 0);
  let c_payment: number = strings.toNumber(state.paymentText, 0);
  let c_rate: number = share(share(c_apr, 100), 12);
  let c_months: number = c_monthsToPayoff(c_balance, c_rate, c_payment);
  let c_children: ui.View[] = [];
  if (c_months < 0) {
    c_children.push(ui.InsetBanner("warning", "Payment too low", "At this payment the balance never clears. Raise the monthly payment.", "", "", "warning"));
  } else {
    let c_interest: number = c_totalInterest(c_balance, c_rate, c_payment, c_months);
    c_children.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.NumberStat("accent", "Months to payoff", c_months, "", "", 1, "at " + ui.formatNumber(c_payment, 2) + " a month", "calendar"),
      ui.NumberStat("warning", "Total interest", c_interest, "$", "", 1, "over the life of the loan", "chart")
    ]));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "", "", c_children));
}
</view>

- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.

- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.

<functions>
function c_ln(x: number): number {
  if (x <= 0) { return 0; }
  let y: number = (x - 1) / (x + 1);
  let y2: number = y * y;
  let term: number = y;
  let sum: number = 0;
  let k: number = 0;
  while (k < 40) {
    sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1);
    term = term * y2;
    k = k + 1;
  }
  return 2 * sum;
}

function c_monthsToPayoff(balance: number, monthlyRate: number, payment: number): number {
  if (balance <= 0) { return 0; }
  if (payment <= 0) { return -1; }
  if (monthlyRate <= 0) {
    return math.ceil(balance / payment);
  }
  let ratio: number = (balance * monthlyRate) / payment;
  if (ratio >= 1) { return -1; }
  let denom: number = c_ln(1 + monthlyRate);
  if (denom === 0) { return -1; }
  let raw: number = -c_ln(1 - ratio) / denom;
  return math.ceil(raw);
}

function c_monthName(m: number): string {
  if (m === 1) { return "January"; }
  if (m === 2) { return "February"; }
  if (m === 3) { return "March"; }
  if (m === 4) { return "April"; }
  if (m === 5) { return "May"; }
  if (m === 6) { return "June"; }
  if (m === 7) { return "July"; }
  if (m === 8) { return "August"; }
  if (m === 9) { return "September"; }
  if (m === 10) { return "October"; }
  if (m === 11) { return "November"; }
  return "December";
}
</functions>

  let c_months: number = c_monthsToPayoff(c_balance, c_rate, c_payment);
  let c_children: ui.View[] = [];
  if (c_months < 0) {
    c_children.push(ui.InsetBanner("warning", "Payment too low", "At this payment the balance never clears. Raise the monthly payment.", "", "", "warning"));
  } else {
    let c_totalMonths: number = time.monthOfYear() - 1 + c_months;
    let c_year: number = time.year() + math.floor(c_totalMonths / 12);
    let c_month: number = c_totalMonths % 12 + 1;
    c_children.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.NumberStat("accent", "Months to payoff", c_months, "", "", 1, "at " + ui.formatNumber(c_payment, 2) + " a month", "calendar"),
      ui.Stat("default", "Payoff date", c_monthName(c_month) + " " + ui.numberToString(c_year), "last payment month", "calendar")
    ]));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "", "", c_children));
}
</view>

function c_monthlyPayment(state: AppState): number {
  let loanAmount: number = strings.toNumber(state.loanAmountText, 0);
  let annualRate: number = strings.toNumber(state.annualRateText, 0);
  let termYears: number = state.termYears;
  let monthlyRate: number = share(annualRate, 1200);
  if (loanAmount <= 0 || termYears <= 0) { return 0; }
  if (monthlyRate === 0) { return share(loanAmount, termYears * 12); }
  return share(loanAmount * monthlyRate, 1 - math.pow(1 + monthlyRate, (0 - termYears) * 12));
}

function c_yearOneInterest(state: AppState): number {
  let loanAmount: number = strings.toNumber(state.loanAmountText, 0);
  let annualRate: number = strings.toNumber(state.annualRateText, 0);
  let termYears: number = state.termYears;
  if (loanAmount <= 0 || termYears <= 0) { return 0; }
  let monthlyRate: number = share(annualRate, 1200);
  let payment: number = c_monthlyPayment(state);
  let balance: number = loanAmount;
  let interest: number = 0;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < 12) {
    let monthInterest: number = balance * monthlyRate;
    interest = interest + monthInterest;
    let principalPart: number = payment - monthInterest;
    if (principalPart > balance) { principalPart = balance; }
    balance = balance - principalPart;
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return interest;
}

function c_yearOnePrincipal(state: AppState): number {
  let loanAmount: number = strings.toNumber(state.loanAmountText, 0);
  let termYears: number = state.termYears;
  if (loanAmount <= 0 || termYears <= 0) { return 0; }
  let payment: number = c_monthlyPayment(state);
  let paid: number = payment * 12;
  let principal: number = paid - c_yearOneInterest(state);
  if (principal < 0) { return 0; }
  if (principal > loanAmount) { return loanAmount; }
  return principal;
}

@jsonable
class AppState {

  paymentText: string;

function share(a: number, b: number): number {
  if (b === 0) { return 0; }
  return a / b;
}



function set_balance(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {balanceText: value, rateText: state.rateText, paymentText: state.paymentText};
}

function set_rate(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {rateText: value, balanceText: state.balanceText, paymentText: state.paymentText};
}

function set_payment(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {paymentText: value, balanceText: state.balanceText, rateText: state.rateText};
}







function view(state: AppState): ui.View {
  let sections: ui.View[] = [];
  sections.push(ui.Header("default", "Loan Payoff", "LOAN TRACKER", "See your balance shrink month by month", ""));

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.

    ui.When(c_short, ui.InsetBanner("danger", "Payment too low", "Your payment of $" + ui.formatNumber(c_payment, 2) + " is less than this month's interest of $" + ui.formatNumber(c_firstInterest, 2) + ". The balance would grow, not shrink. Raise the monthly payment above the interest to start paying it down.", "", "", "warning")),
    ui.When(c_months > 0, ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, c_planRows)),
    ui.When(c_months === 0 && !c_short, ui.InsetBanner("warning", "No payoff yet", "Enter a balance and a monthly payment larger than the first month's interest to see the schedule.", "", "", "warning"))
  ]));
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

Request: credit card payoff schedule

The section must do:
- the figure "Months to payoff": how many monthly payments clear the balance (the plan works it out as ceil(-log(1 - balance * monthlyRate / 100 / payment) / log(1 + monthlyRate / 100)); for balance = 5000, monthlyRate = 1.8333333333333333, payment = 250 that is 26)
- the figure "Total interest": all the interest paid over the payoff (money: show it with its currency sign $) (the plan works it out as monthsToPayoff * payment - balance; for monthsToPayoff = 26, payment = 250, balance = 5000 that is 1500)
- the figure "Total paid": payments plus the balance cleared (money: show it with its currency sign $) (the plan works it out as monthsToPayoff * payment; for monthsToPayoff = 26, payment = 250 that is 6500)

The person sets these on the screen and nothing else uses them yet; the section uses them:
- "Card balance": state.balanceText (the number as typed; strings.toNumber reads it)
- "Monthly payment": state.paymentText (the number as typed; strings.toNumber reads it)

Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.

Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.

function c_log(x: number): number {

<functions>
function c_log(x: number): number {
  if (x <= 0) { return 0; }
  let y: number = x - 1;
  let term: number = y;
  let sum: number = 0;
  let k: number = 1;
  while (k <= 40) {
    sum = sum + term / k;
    term = term * y;
    k = k + 1;
  }
  return sum;
}

function c_monthsFor(balance: number, rate: number, payment: number): number {
  if (balance <= 0) { return 0; }
  if (payment <= 0) { return 0; }
  if (rate <= 0) { return math.ceil(balance / payment); }
  let inner: number = 1 - balance * rate / payment;
  if (inner <= 0) { return 0; }
  let denom: number = c_log(1 + rate);
  if (denom === 0) { return 0; }
  return math.ceil(c_log(inner) / denom);
}

function c_setSavingsView(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {c_savingsView: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

{
  let c_balance: number = strings.toNumber(state.loanBalanceText, 0);
  let c_apr: number = strings.toNumber(state.aprText, 0);
  let c_payment: number = strings.toNumber(state.monthlyPaymentText, 0);
  let c_extra: number = strings.toNumber(state.extraPaymentText, 0);
  let c_rate: number = share(share(c_apr, 100), 12);
  let c_total: number = c_payment + c_extra;
  let c_months: number = c_monthsFor(c_balance, c_rate, c_total);
  let c_baseMonths: number = c_monthsFor(c_balance, c_rate, c_payment);
  let c_monthsSaved: number = c_baseMonths - c_months;
  if (c_monthsSaved < 0) { c_monthsSaved = 0; }
  let c_interestPaid: number = c_months * c_total - c_balance;
  if (c_interestPaid < 0) { c_interestPaid = 0; }
  let c_baseInterest: number = c_baseMonths * c_payment - c_balance;
  if (c_baseInterest < 0) { c_baseInterest = 0; }
  let c_interestSaved: number = c_baseInterest - c_interestPaid;
  if (c_interestSaved < 0) { c_interestSaved = 0; }
  let c_valid: boolean = c_balance > 0 && c_total > 0 && c_months > 0;
  let c_interestSavedShown: number = c_interestSaved;
  let c_monthsSavedShown: number = c_monthsSaved;
  let c_periodLabel: string = "per month";
  if (state.c_savingsView === 1) {
    c_interestSavedShown = c_interestSaved * 12;
    c_monthsSavedShown = c_monthsSaved * 12;
    c_periodLabel = "per year";
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "Savings", "What the extra payment saves you, " + c_periodLabel, [
    ui.Select("default", "Show savings", ["Monthly", "Yearly"], state.c_savingsView, "c_setSavingsView"),
    ui.When(c_valid, ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.NumberStat("success", "Interest saved", c_interestSavedShown, "$", "", 1, "", "star", 2),
      ui.NumberStat("default", "Months saved", c_monthsSavedShown, "", "", 1, "", "minus")
    ])),
    ui.When(!c_valid, ui.InsetBanner("warning", "Enter your loan details", "Add a loan balance and a monthly payment above to see the savings.", "", "", "warning"))
  ]));
}
</view>

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

  animal: number;
  faceUp: boolean;

<functions>
function c_animalEmoji(id: number): string {
  if (id === 0) { return "🐄"; }
  if (id === 1) { return "🐖"; }
  if (id === 2) { return "🐑"; }
  if (id === 3) { return "🐔"; }
  if (id === 4) { return "🐴"; }
  if (id === 5) { return "🦆"; }
  if (id === 6) { return "🐐"; }
  if (id === 7) { return "🦢"; }
  if (id === 8) { return "🐴"; }
  if (id === 9) { return "🐈"; }
  if (id === 10) { return "🐕"; }
  return "🐇";
}

function c_build(pairs: number, seed: number): C_Card[] {
  let n: number = pairs * 2;
  let ids: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < pairs) {
    ids.push(i);
    ids.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let s: number = seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    s = math.randomStep(s);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(s, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = ids[j];
    ids[j] = ids[k];
    ids[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  let out: C_Card[] = [];
  let m: number = 0;
  while (m < n) {
    out.push({animal: ids[m], faceUp: false, matched: false});
    m = m + 1;
  }
  return out;
}

function c_newGame(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let seed: number = math.randomStep(state.c_seed);
  let cards: C_Card[] = c_build(state.pairs, seed);
  return {c_cards: cards, c_pairs: state.pairs, c_flips: 0, c_matched: 0, c_first: -1, c_second: -1, c_waiting: false, c_seed: seed, c_won: false, c_round: state.c_round + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_tap(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_won) {
    return c_newGame(state, 0);
  }
  if (state.c_waiting) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  if (state.c_cards.length() === 0) {
    return c_newGame(state, 0);
  }
  if (value < 0 || value >= state.c_cards.length()) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let card: C_Card = state.c_cards[value];
  if (card.faceUp || card.matched) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let cards: C_Card[] = [];
  for (let c: C_Card of state.c_cards) {
    cards.push({animal: c.animal, faceUp: c.faceUp, matched: c.matched});
  }
  let flipped: C_Card = cards[value];
  flipped.faceUp = true;
  cards[value] = flipped;
  let flips: number = state.c_flips + 1;
  if (state.c_first < 0) {
    return {c_cards: cards, c_flips: flips, c_first: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let a: C_Card = cards[state.c_first];
  if (a.animal === flipped.animal) {
    a.matched = true;
    cards[state.c_first] = a;
    let b: C_Card = cards[value];
    b.matched = true;
    cards[value] = b;
    let matched: number = state.c_matched + 1;
    let won: boolean = matched >= state.c_pairs;
    return {c_cards: cards, c_flips: flips, c_matched: matched, c_first: -1, c_second: -1, c_waiting: false, c_won: won__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_cards: cards, c_flips: flips, c_second: value, c_waiting: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_resolve(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_waiting) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let cards: C_Card[] = [];
  for (let c: C_Card of state.c_cards) {
    cards.push({animal: c.animal, faceUp: c.faceUp, matched: c.matched});
  }
  if (state.c_first >= 0 && state.c_first < cards.length()) {
    let a: C_Card = cards[state.c_first];
    a.faceUp = false;
    cards[state.c_first] = a;
  }
  if (state.c_second >= 0 && state.c_second < cards.length()) {
    let b: C_Card = cards[state.c_second];
    b.faceUp = false;
    cards[state.c_second] = b;
  }
  return {c_cards: cards, c_first: -1, c_second: -1, c_waiting: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>
@jsonable
class C_Card {
  animal: number;
  faceUp: boolean;
  matched: boolean;
}
</classes>
<fields>
c_cards: C_Card[] = []
c_flips: number = 0
c_matched: number = 0
c_first: number = -1
c_second: number = -1
c_waiting: boolean = false
c_seed: number = 7
c_won: boolean = false
c_round: number = 0
</fields>
<functions>
function c_animalName(id: number): string {
  if (id === 0) { return "Cow"; }
  if (id === 1) { return "Pig"; }
  if (id === 2) { return "Sheep"; }
  if (id === 3) { return "Hen"; }
  if (id === 4) { return "Horse"; }
  if (id === 5) { return "Duck"; }
  if (id === 6) { return "Goat"; }
  if (id === 7) { return "Goose"; }
  if (id === 8) { return "Donkey"; }
  if (id === 9) { return "Cat"; }
  if (id === 10) { return "Dog"; }
  return "Rabbit";
}

function c_build(pairs: number, seed: number): C_Card[] {
  let n: number = pairs * 2;
  let ids: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < pairs) {
    ids.push(i);
    ids.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let s: number = seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    s = math.randomStep(s);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(s, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = ids[j];
    ids[j] = ids[k];
    ids[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  let out: C_Card[] = [];
  let m: number = 0;
  while (m < n) {
    out.push({animal: ids[m], faceUp: false, matched: false});
    m = m + 1;
  }
  return out;
}

function c_newGame(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let seed: number = math.randomStep(state.c_seed);
  let cards: C_Card[] = c_build(state.pairs, seed);
  return {c_cards: cards, c_flips: 0, c_matched: 0, c_first: -1, c_second: -1, c_waiting: false, c_seed: seed, c_won: false, c_round: state.c_round + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_tap(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_won) {
    return c_newGame(state, 0);
  }
  if (state.c_waiting) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  if (state.c_cards.length() === 0) {
    return c_newGame(state, 0);
  }
  if (value < 0 || value >= state.c_cards.length()) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let card: C_Card = state.c_cards[value];
  if (card.faceUp || card.matched) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let cards: C_Card[] = [];
  for (let c: C_Card of state.c_cards) {
    cards.push({animal: c.animal, faceUp: c.faceUp, matched: c.matched});
  }
  let flipped: C_Card = cards[value];
  flipped.faceUp = true;
  cards[value] = flipped;
  let flips: number = state.c_flips + 1;
  if (state.c_first < 0) {
    return {c_cards: cards, c_flips: flips, c_first: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let a: C_Card = cards[state.c_first];
  if (a.animal === flipped.animal) {
    a.matched = true;
    cards[state.c_first] = a;
    let b: C_Card = cards[value];
    b.matched = true;
    cards[value] = b;
    let matched: number = state.c_matched + 1;
    let won: boolean = matched >= state.pairs;
    return {c_cards: cards, c_flips: flips, c_matched: matched, c_first: -1, c_second: -1, c_waiting: false, c_won: won__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_cards: cards, c_flips: flips, c_second: value, c_waiting: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_resolve(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_waiting) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let cards: C_Card[] = [];
  for (let c: C_Card of state.c_cards) {
    cards.push({animal: c.animal, faceUp: c.faceUp, matched: c.matched});
  }
  if (state.c_first >= 0 && state.c_first < cards.length()) {
    let a: C_Card = cards[state.c_first];
    a.faceUp = false;
    cards[state.c_first] = a;
  }
  if (state.c_second >= 0 && state.c_second < cards.length()) {
    let b: C_Card = cards[state.c_second];
    b.faceUp = false;
    cards[state.c_second] = b;
  }
  return {c_cards: cards, c_first: -1, c_second: -1, c_waiting: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let cards: ui.View[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.c_cards.length()) {
    let card: C_Card = state.c_cards[i];
    let label: string = "";
    if (card.faceUp || card.matched) {
      label = c_animalName(card.animal);
    } else {
      label = "?";
    }
    let tone: string = "default";
    if (card.matched) {
      tone = "success";
    } else if (card.faceUp) {
      tone = "accent";
    }
    cards.push(ui.Cell(tone, label, "c_tap", i, true));
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let cols: number = 4;
  if (state.pairs <= 2) { cols = 2; }
  else if (state.pairs <= 4) { cols = 3; }
  else if (state.pairs <= 8) { cols = 4; }
  else { cols = 5; }
  let started: boolean = state.c_cards.length() > 0;
  let board: ui.View[] = [];
  if (started) {
    board.push(ui.Grid("default", cols, cards));
  } else {
    board.push(ui.EmptyState("default", "Ready to play", "Start a game to lay out the cards.", "Start game", "c_newGame", "star"));
  }
  let status: ui.View[] = [];
  if (started) {
    status.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, [
