messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>
c_words: string[] = ["apple", "brisk", "candid", "dwell", "eager", "fable", "grasp", "humble", "ivory", "jolly", "kneel", "lucid", "mellow", "nimble", "orbit", "placid", "quaint", "rustic", "subtle", "tender"]
c_index: number = 0
c_typed: string = ""
c_correct: number = 0
c_attempts: number = 0
c_wrong: boolean = false
c_done: boolean = false
c_seed: number = 7
</fields>
<functions>
function c_currentWord(state: AppState): string {
  if (state.c_index >= state.c_words.length()) { return ""; }
  return state.c_words[state.c_index];
}

function c_onType(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_typed: value, c_wrong: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onCheck(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_done) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let target: string = c_currentWord(state);
  if (target === "") { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let guess: string = strings.trim(strings.toLowerCase(state.c_typed));
  if (guess === "") { return {c_wrong: true__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let attempts: number = state.c_attempts + 1;
  if (guess === strings.toLowerCase(target)) {
    let nextIndex: number = state.c_index + 1;
    let done: boolean = nextIndex >= state.c_words.length() || nextIndex >= state.wordCount;
    return {c_index: nextIndex, c_typed: "", c_correct: state.c_correct + 1, c_attempts: attempts, c_wrong: false, c_done: done__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_attempts: attempts, c_wrong: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onSkip(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_done) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let nextIndex: number = state.c_index + 1;
  let done: boolean = nextIndex >= state.c_words.length() || nextIndex >= state.wordCount;
  return {c_index: nextIndex, c_typed: "", c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_wrong: false, c_done: done__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onRestart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_index: 0, c_typed: "", c_correct: 0, c_attempts: 0, c_wrong: false, c_done: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onShuffle(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let seed: number = state.c_seed + 1;
  let out: string[] = [];
  for (let w: string of state.c_words) {
    out.push(w);
  }
  let n: number = out.length();
  let i: number = n - 1;
  while (i > 0) {
    let r: number = math.randomBelow(seed, i + 1);
    seed = math.randomStep(seed);
    let tmp: string = out[i];
    out[i] = out[r];
    out[r] = tmp;
    i = i - 1;
  }
  return {c_words: out, c_seed: seed, c_index: 0, c_typed: "", c_correct: 0, c_attempts: 0, c_wrong: false, c_done: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_wpm(state: AppState): number {
  let seconds: number = state.elapsedMs / 1000;
  if (seconds <= 0) { return 0; }
  return state.c_correct / (seconds / 60);
}

function c_accuracy(state: AppState): number {
  let denom: number = math.max(state.c_correct + 1, 1);
  return state.c_correct / denom * 100;
}
</functions>
<view>
let c_target: string = c_currentWord(state);
let c_typedCount: number = state.c_correct;
let c_wpmValue: number = c_wpm(state);
let c_accValue: number = c_accuracy(state);
let c_goal: number = state.wordCount;
let c_children: ui.View[] = [];
if (state.c_done) {
  c_children.push(ui.InsetBanner("success", "Drill complete", "You typed " + ui.numberToString(c_typedCount) + " words correctly.", "", "", "check"));
} else {
  c_children.push(ui.Text("eyebrow", "Word " + ui.numberToString(state.c_index + 1) + " of " + ui.numberToString(c_goal)));
  c_children.push(ui.Text("display", c_target));
  c_children.push(ui.TextField("default", "Type the word", state.c_typed, "c_onType"));
  c_children.push(ui.When(state.c_wrong, ui.Text("danger", "Not quite — check the spelling and try again.")));
  c_children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [
    ui.Button("primary", "Check", "c_onCheck", 0, true),
    ui.Button("secondary", "Skip", "c_onSkip", 0, true)
  ]));
}
c_children.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, [
  ui.NumberStat("default", "Words typed", c_typedCount, "", "", 1, "of " + ui.numberToString(c_goal), "check"),
  ui.NumberStat("accent", "Words per minute", c_wpmValue, "", "", 1, "", "chart"),
  ui.NumberStat("default", "Accuracy", c_accValue, "", "%", 1, "", "star")
]));
c_children.push(ui.Progress("accent", "Words typed", c_typedCount, c_goal));
c_children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [
  ui.Button("secondary", "Shuffle words", "c_onShuffle", 0, true),
  ui.When(state.c_done, ui.Button("secondary", "Type again", "c_onRestart", 0, true))
]));
sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Typing drill", "Type each word exactly, then tap Check", c_children));
</view>

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

Request: timed vocabulary word typing drill

The section must do:
- A list of vocabulary words for the person to type, one at a time, with the next word shown after each is typed correctly; the phone checks each typed word against the shown one and moves on.
- the figure "Words typed": How many vocabulary words the person has typed correctly so far (the plan works it out as entryCount; for entryCount = 7 that is 7)
- the figure "Words per minute": Typing speed in correct words per minute (the plan works it out as entryCount / (elapsed / 60); for entryCount = 7, elapsed = 42 that is 10)
- the figure "Accuracy": Share of typed words that were correct on the first try (a percent: show it with the % sign) (the plan works it out as entryCount / max(entryCount + 1, 1) * 100; for entryCount = 9 that is 90)

The person sets these on the screen and nothing else uses them yet; the section uses them:
- "Words per drill": state.wordCount

The program already has these: use them, do not make your own:
- a clock (a countdown): state.elapsedMs is the milliseconds passed, state.running whether it runs, state.finished whether it ended. Its Start, Stop and Reset buttons and its Ticker are already on the screen and drive it: the section draws no timer, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no Ticker of its own, and keeps no clock state of its own; it reads state.elapsedMs and countdownSeconds(state), the length in seconds.

Nothing they show is shown again: no second list, total, chart, Remove last or Start over button. While what the section works from is still empty, it shows one plain line saying what will appear and when, never a ui.EmptyState: the list above already has one (two empty states one under the other read as a broken screen).

import * as ui from "std/ui"

@jsonable
class AppState {
  elapsedMs: number;
  running: boolean;
  finished: boolean;
  drillLengthIndex: number;
  wordCount: number;
}

function init(): AppState {
  return {elapsedMs: 0, running: false, finished: false, drillLengthIndex: 1, wordCount: 10};
}

function countdownSeconds(state: AppState): number {
  let drillLengthValues: number[] = [60, 120, 180];
  let drillLength: number = drillLengthValues[state.drillLengthIndex];
  let wordCount: number = state.wordCount;
  let secondsPerMinute: number = 60;
  return drillLength;
}

function onTick(state: AppState, elapsedMs: number): AppState {
  if (!state.running) { return state; }
  let total: number = countdownSeconds(state) * 1000;
  let next: number = state.elapsedMs + elapsedMs;
  if (next < total) { return {elapsedMs: next, running: state.running, finished: state.finished, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex, wordCount: state.wordCount}; }
  return {elapsedMs: total, running: false, finished: true, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex, wordCount: state.wordCount};
}

function onStart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let startAt: number = state.elapsedMs;
  if (state.finished) { startAt = 0; }
  return {running: true, finished: false, elapsedMs: startAt, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex, wordCount: state.wordCount};
}

function onStop(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {running: false, elapsedMs: state.elapsedMs, finished: state.finished, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex, wordCount: state.wordCount};
}

function onReset(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {running: false, finished: false, elapsedMs: 0, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex, wordCount: state.wordCount};
}

function share(a: number, b: number): number {
  if (b === 0) { return 0; }
  return a / b;
}



function set_drillLength(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {drillLengthIndex: value, elapsedMs: 0, running: false, finished: false, wordCount: state.wordCount};
}

function set_wordCount(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {wordCount: value, elapsedMs: state.elapsedMs, running: state.running, finished: state.finished, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex};
}







function view(state: AppState): ui.View {
  let sections: ui.View[] = [];
  sections.push(ui.Header("default", "Vocab Typing Drill", "TYPING DRILL", "Type each word before the clock runs out", "clock"));
  {
    sections.push(ui.Ticker("default", "clock", 200, state.running, "onTick"));
      let drillLengthValues: number[] = [60, 120, 180];
      let drillLength: number = drillLengthValues[state.drillLengthIndex];
      let wordCount: number = state.wordCount;
      let secondsPerMinute: number = 60;
      let duration: number = countdownSeconds(state);
      let elapsed: number = math.min(state.elapsedMs / 1000, duration);

  if (state.c_done) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let target: string = c_currentWord(state);
  if (target === "") { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let guess: string = strings.trim(strings.toLowerCase(state.c_typed));
  if (guess === "") { return {c_wrong: true__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let attempts: number = state.c_attempts + 1;

    let done: boolean = nextIndex >= state.c_words.length() || nextIndex >= state.wordCount;
    return {c_index: nextIndex, c_typed: "", c_correct: state.c_correct + 1, c_attempts: attempts, c_wrong: false, c_done: done__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_attempts: attempts, c_wrong: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>
c_typed: number = 0
c_input: string = ""
c_wrong: boolean = false
c_streak: number = 0
c_best: number = 0
</fields>
<functions>
function c_animals(): string[] {
  let names: string[] = ["cat", "dog", "horse", "rabbit", "tiger", "elephant", "monkey", "penguin", "dolphin", "giraffe", "zebra", "lion", "bear", "wolf", "sheep", "goat", "camel", "otter", "badger", "falcon", "parrot", "turtle", "salmon", "beaver", "donkey", "panda", "koala", "lemur", "hyena", "jaguar"];
  return names;
}

function c_current(state: AppState): string {
  let names: string[] = c_animals();
  let n: number = names.length();
  let idx: number = state.c_typed % n;
  return names[idx];
}

function c_onType(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  let target: string = c_current(state);
  let typed: string = strings.trim(value);
  if (strings.toLowerCase(typed) === strings.toLowerCase(target)) {
    let nextStreak: number = state.c_streak + 1;
    let nextBest: number = state.c_best;
    if (nextStreak > nextBest) { nextBest = nextStreak; }
    return {c_typed: state.c_typed + 1, c_input: "", c_wrong: false, c_streak: nextStreak, c_best: nextBest__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_input: value, c_wrong: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_check(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let target: string = c_current(state);
  let typed: string = strings.trim(state.c_input);
  if (strings.toLowerCase(typed) === strings.toLowerCase(target)) {
    let nextStreak: number = state.c_streak + 1;
    let nextBest: number = state.c_best;
    if (nextStreak > nextBest) { nextBest = nextStreak; }
    return {c_typed: state.c_typed + 1, c_input: "", c_wrong: false, c_streak: nextStreak, c_best: nextBest__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_wrong: true, c_streak: 0__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_skip(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_input: "", c_wrong: false, c_streak: 0__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_wpm(state: AppState): number {
  let seconds: number = state.elapsedMs / 1000;
  if (seconds <= 0) { return 0; }
  return state.c_typed / (seconds / 60);
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let c_target: string = c_current(state);
  let c_seconds: number = state.elapsedMs / 1000;
  let c_wpmValue: number = c_wpm(state);
  let c_rows: ui.View[] = [];
  c_rows.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, [
    ui.NumberStat("accent", "Animals typed", state.c_typed, "", "", 1, "correct names", "check"),
    ui.NumberStat("success", "Streak", state.c_streak, "", "", 1, "in a row", "star"),
    ui.NumberStat("default", "Words per minute", c_wpmValue, "", "", 1, "names per minute", "chart")
  ]));
  if (state.finished) {
    c_rows.push(ui.InsetBanner("success", "Drill complete", "You typed " + ui.numberToString(state.c_typed) + " animal names in " + ui.durationToString(math.round(c_seconds)) + ". Best streak: " + ui.numberToString(state.c_best) + ".", "", "", "check"));
  } else if (!state.running && state.elapsedMs === 0) {
    c_rows.push(ui.Text("body", "Press Start above, then type each animal name as it appears."));
  }
  if (state.running || state.elapsedMs > 0) {
    c_rows.push(ui.Text("display", c_target));
    c_rows.push(ui.TextField("default", "Type the animal name", state.c_input, "c_onType", "", false, "", 0, "", 40, ""));
    if (state.c_wrong) {
      c_rows.push(ui.Text("danger", "Not quite — check the spelling and try again."));
    }
    c_rows.push(ui.ActionBar("spread", [
      ui.Button("primary", "Check", "c_check", 0, state.running),
      ui.Button("secondary", "Skip", "c_skip", 0, state.running)
    ]));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Speed drill", "Type each animal name exactly", c_rows));
}
</view>

Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.

- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.

- the figure "Animals typed": How many animal names were typed correctly before the drill ended (the plan works it out as entryCount; for entryCount = 18 that is 18)
- the figure "Words per minute": Correctly typed animal names per minute of the drill (the plan works it out as wordsTyped / (drillLength / secondsPerMinute); for wordsTyped = 18, drillLength = 60, secondsPerMinute = 60 that is 18)

The person sets these on the screen and nothing else uses them yet; the section uses them:
- "Drill length": state.drillLengthIndex (the index of the chosen option: 30 seconds, 60 seconds, 90 seconds, 120 seconds)

The program already has these: use them, do not make your own:
- a clock (a countdown): state.elapsedMs is the milliseconds passed, state.running whether it runs, state.finished whether it ended. Its Start, Stop and Reset buttons and its Ticker are already on the screen and drive it: the section draws no timer, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no Ticker of its own, and keeps no clock state of its own; it reads state.elapsedMs and countdownSeconds(state), the length in seconds.

Nothing they show is shown again: no second list, total, chart, Remove last or Start over button. While what the section works from is still empty, it shows one plain line saying what will appear and when, never a ui.EmptyState: the list above already has one (two empty states one under the other read as a broken screen).

  let drillLength: number = drillLengthValues[state.drillLengthIndex];
  let secondsPerMinute: number = 60;
  return drillLength;
}

function onTick(state: AppState, elapsedMs: number): AppState {
  if (!state.running) { return state; }
  let total: number = countdownSeconds(state) * 1000;
  let next: number = state.elapsedMs + elapsedMs;
  if (next < total) { return {elapsedMs: next, running: state.running, finished: state.finished, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex}; }
  return {elapsedMs: total, running: false, finished: true, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex};
}

function onStart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let startAt: number = state.elapsedMs;
  if (state.finished) { startAt = 0; }
  return {running: true, finished: false, elapsedMs: startAt, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex};
}

function onStop(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {running: false, elapsedMs: state.elapsedMs, finished: state.finished, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex};
}

function onReset(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {running: false, finished: false, elapsedMs: 0, drillLengthIndex: state.drillLengthIndex};
}

function share(a: number, b: number): number {
  if (b === 0) { return 0; }

}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

</fields>
<functions>
function c_shuffle(state: AppState): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_titles.length();
  let order: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    order.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    seed = math.randomStep(seed);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(seed, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = order[j];
    order[j] = order[k];
    order[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  return {c_order: order, c_pos: 0, c_typed: "", c_correct: 0, c_attempts: 0, c_hasLast: false, c_lastOk: false, c_lastTitle: "", c_seed: seed, c_hint: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onType(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_typed: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_submit(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let ok: boolean = strings.trim(state.c_typed).toLowerCase() === target.toLowerCase();
  let correct: number = state.c_correct;
  if (ok) {
    correct = correct + 1;
  }
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {
    nextPos = 0;
  }
  return {c_correct: correct, c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_pos: nextPos, c_typed: "", c_lastOk: ok, c_hasLast: true, c_lastTitle: target, c_hint: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_skip(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {
    nextPos = 0;
  }
  return {c_pos: nextPos, c_typed: "", c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_lastOk: false, c_hasLast: true, c_lastTitle: target, c_hint: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_reshuffle(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_shuffle(state);
}

function c_showHint(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_hint: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_wpm(state: AppState): number {
  let duration: number = countdownSeconds(state);
  let minutes: number = duration / 60;
  if (minutes <= 0) {
    return 0;
  }
  return math.round(state.c_correct / minutes);
}

function c_accuracy(state: AppState): number {
  let denom: number = state.c_attempts;
  if (denom < 1) {
    denom = 1;
  }
  return math.round(100 * state.c_correct / denom);
}
</functions>
<view>

  let current: string = "";
  if (n > 0) {
    current = state.c_titles[state.c_order[state.c_pos % n]];
  }
  let stats: ui.View[] = [];
  stats.push(ui.NumberStat("default", "Words typed", state.c_correct, "", "", 1, "correct titles", "check"));
  stats.push(ui.NumberStat("accent", "Accuracy", c_accuracy(state), "", "%", 1, "of " + ui.numberToString(state.c_attempts) + " typed", "chart"));

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<functions>
function c_shuffle(state: AppState): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_titles.length();
  let order: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    order.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    seed = math.randomStep(seed);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(seed, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = order[j];
    order[j] = order[k];
    order[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  return {c_order: order, c_pos: 0, c_typed: "", c_correct: 0, c_attempts: 0, c_hasLast: false, c_lastOk: false, c_lastTitle: "", c_seed: seed__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onType(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_typed: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_submit(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let ok: boolean = strings.trim(state.c_typed).toLowerCase() === target.toLowerCase();
  let correct: number = state.c_correct;
  if (ok) {
    correct = correct + 1;
  }
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {
    nextPos = 0;
  }
  return {c_correct: correct, c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_pos: nextPos, c_typed: "", c_lastOk: ok, c_hasLast: true, c_lastTitle: target__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_skip(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {
    nextPos = 0;
  }
  return {c_pos: nextPos, c_typed: "", c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_lastOk: false, c_hasLast: true, c_lastTitle: target__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_reshuffle(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_shuffle(state);
}

function c_arm(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_armed: true, c_countdownMs: 3000__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_countTick(state: AppState, elapsedMs: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_armed) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let next: number = state.c_countdownMs - elapsedMs;
  if (next <= 0) {
    return {c_armed: false, c_countdownMs: 0, c_typed: "", c_correct: 0, c_attempts: 0, c_hasLast: false, c_lastOk: false, c_lastTitle: "", running: true, finished: false, elapsedMs: 0__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  return {c_countdownMs: next__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_wpm(state: AppState): number {
  let duration: number = countdownSeconds(state);
  let minutes: number = duration / 60;
  if (minutes <= 0) {
    return 0;
  }
  return math.round(state.c_correct / minutes);
}

function c_accuracy(state: AppState): number {
  let denom: number = state.c_attempts;
  if (denom < 1) {
    denom = 1;
  }
  return math.round(100 * state.c_correct / denom);
}

<functions>
function c_shuffle(state: AppState): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_titles.length();
  let order: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    order.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    seed = math.randomStep(seed);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(seed, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = order[j];
    order[j] = order[k];
    order[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  return {c_order: order, c_pos: 0, c_typed: "", c_correct: 0, c_attempts: 0, c_hasLast: false, c_lastOk: false, c_lastTitle: "", c_seed: seed__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onType(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_typed: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_submit(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let ok: boolean = strings.trim(state.c_typed).toLowerCase() === target.toLowerCase();
  let correct: number = state.c_correct;
  if (ok) {
    correct = correct + 1;
  }
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {
    nextPos = 0;
  }
  return {c_correct: correct, c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_pos: nextPos, c_typed: "", c_lastOk: ok, c_hasLast: true, c_lastTitle: target__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_skip(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {

  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {

}

Request: typing test with famous book titles

The section must do:
- A shuffled list of famous book titles (e.g. Pride and Prejudice, Moby-Dick, The Great Gatsby, War and Peace, Jane Eyre, 1984, To Kill a Mockingbird, The Hobbit) shown one at a time; the person types each title into a text box, the phone marks it correct or wrong and moves to the next title, and the list keeps cycling until time runs out.
- the figure "Words typed": how many titles were typed correctly, each counted as one word (the plan works it out as entryCount; for entryCount = 7 that is 7)
- the figure "Accuracy": share of typed titles that were correct (a percent: show it with the % sign) (the plan works it out as round(100 * wordsTyped / max(1, entryCount)); for wordsTyped = 7, entryCount = 10 that is 70)
- the figure "Words per minute": correct titles per minute of the test (the plan works it out as round(wordsTyped / (duration / 60)); for wordsTyped = 7, duration = 60 that is 7)

The program already has these: use them, do not make your own:
- a clock (a countdown): state.elapsedMs is the milliseconds passed, state.running whether it runs, state.finished whether it ended. Its Start, Stop and Reset buttons and its Ticker are already on the screen and drive it: the section draws no timer, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no Ticker of its own, and keeps no clock state of its own; it reads state.elapsedMs and countdownSeconds(state), the length in seconds.

Nothing they show is shown again: no second list, total, chart, Remove last or Start over button. While what the section works from is still empty, it shows one plain line saying what will appear and when, never a ui.EmptyState: the list above already has one (two empty states one under the other read as a broken screen).

import * as ui from "std/ui"

@jsonable
class AppState {
  elapsedMs: number;
  running: boolean;
  finished: boolean;
  durationItemIndex: number;
}

function init(): AppState {
  return {elapsedMs: 0, running: false, finished: false, durationItemIndex: 1};
}

function countdownSeconds(state: AppState): number {
  let durationItemValues: number[] = [15, 30, 60, 120];
  let durationItem: number = durationItemValues[state.durationItemIndex];
  let charsPerWord: number = 5;
  return durationItem;
}

function onTick(state: AppState, elapsedMs: number): AppState {
  if (!state.running) { return state; }
  let total: number = countdownSeconds(state) * 1000;
  let next: number = state.elapsedMs + elapsedMs;
  if (next < total) { return {elapsedMs: next, running: state.running, finished: state.finished, durationItemIndex: state.durationItemIndex}; }
  return {elapsedMs: total, running: false, finished: true, durationItemIndex: state.durationItemIndex};
}

function onStart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let startAt: number = state.elapsedMs;
  if (state.finished) { startAt = 0; }
  return {running: true, finished: false, elapsedMs: startAt, durationItemIndex: state.durationItemIndex};
}

function onStop(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {running: false, elapsedMs: state.elapsedMs, finished: state.finished, durationItemIndex: state.durationItemIndex};
}

function onReset(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {running: false, finished: false, elapsedMs: 0, durationItemIndex: state.durationItemIndex};
}

function share(a: number, b: number): number {
  if (b === 0) { return 0; }
  return a / b;
}



function set_durationItem(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {durationItemIndex: value, elapsedMs: 0, running: false, finished: false};
}







function view(state: AppState): ui.View {
  let sections: ui.View[] = [];
  sections.push(ui.Header("default", "Typing Test", "TYPE RACER", "Type famous book titles against the clock", "clock"));
  {
    sections.push(ui.Ticker("default", "clock", 200, state.running, "onTick"));
      let durationItemValues: number[] = [15, 30, 60, 120];
      let durationItem: number = durationItemValues[state.durationItemIndex];
      let charsPerWord: number = 5;
      let duration: number = countdownSeconds(state);
      let elapsed: number = math.min(state.elapsedMs / 1000, duration);

function c_shuffle(state: AppState): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_titles.length();
  let order: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    order.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    seed = math.randomStep(seed);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(seed, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = order[j];
    order[j] = order[k];
    order[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  return {c_order: order, c_pos: 0, c_typed: "", c_correct: 0, c_attempts: 0, c_hasLast: false, c_lastOk: false, c_lastTitle: "", c_seed: seed__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onType(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_typed: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_submit(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let ok: boolean = strings.trim(state.c_typed).toLowerCase() === target.toLowerCase();
  let correct: number = state.c_correct;
  if (ok) {
    correct = correct + 1;
  }
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {
    nextPos = 0;
  }
  return {c_correct: correct, c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_pos: nextPos, c_typed: "", c_lastOk: ok, c_hasLast: true, c_lastTitle: target__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_skip(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.c_order.length();
  if (n === 0) {
    return {__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_pos % n];
  let target: string = state.c_titles[idx];
  let nextPos: number = state.c_pos + 1;
  if (nextPos >= n) {
    nextPos = 0;
  }
  return {c_pos: nextPos, c_typed: "", c_attempts: state.c_attempts + 1, c_lastOk: false, c_hasLast: true, c_lastTitle: target__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_reshuffle(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_shuffle(state);
}

function c_wpm(state: AppState): number {
  let duration: number = countdownSeconds(state);
  let minutes: number = duration / 60;
  if (minutes <= 0) {
    return 0;
  }
  return math.round(state.c_correct / minutes);
}

function c_accuracy(state: AppState): number {
  let denom: number = state.c_attempts;
  if (denom < 1) {
    denom = 1;
  }
  return math.round(100 * state.c_correct / denom);
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");

  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. }

function c_totalNights(state: AppState): number {
  let sum: number = 0;
  for (let r: Tally of state.records7) {
    if (r.amount > 0) { sum = sum + r.amount; }
  }
  return sum;
}

function c_costPerNight(state: AppState): number {
  let nights: number = c_totalNights(state);
  if (nights <= 0) { return 0; }
  let rental: number = strings.toNumber(state.c_rentalC, 0);
  if (rental <= 0) { return 0; }
  return math.round(rental / nights * 100) / 100;
}

function c_myShare(state: AppState): number {
  let nights: number = strings.toNumber(state.c_myNightsC, 0);
  if (nights <= 0) { return 0; }
  return math.round(c_costPerNight(state) * nights * 100) / 100;
}

function c_money(state: AppState, amount: number): string {
  if (state.currency7.length() === 0) { return ui.formatNumber(amount, 2); }
  return state.currency7 + ui.formatNumber(amount, 2);
}
