messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>
c_renameIndex: number = 0;
c_renameText: string = "";
c_renameTouched: boolean = false;
</fields>
<functions>
function c_totalMinutes(state: AppState): number {
  let sum: number = 0;
  for (let r: Tally of state.records8) {
    sum = sum + r.amount;
  }
  return math.round(sum * 100) / 100;
}

function c_costPerMinute(state: AppState): number {
  let monthlyCost: number = strings.toNumber(state.monthlyCostText, 0);
  let minutes: number = c_totalMinutes(state);
  if (minutes <= 0) { return 0; }
  return monthlyCost / minutes;
}

function c_pickRename(state: AppState, index: number): AppState {
  let name: string = "";
  if (index >= 0 && index < state.labels8.length()) {
    name = state.labels8[index];
  }
  return {c_renameIndex: index, c_renameText: name, c_renameTouched: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setRenameText(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_renameText: value, c_renameTouched: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_applyRename(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let trimmed: string = strings.trim(state.c_renameText);
  if (trimmed.length() === 0) {
    return {c_renameTouched: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let out: string[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.labels8.length()) {
    if (i === state.c_renameIndex) {
      out.push(trimmed);
    } else {
      out.push(state.labels8[i]);
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return {labels8: out, c_renameText: trimmed, c_renameTouched: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{

  let monthlyCost: number = strings.toNumber(state.monthlyCostText, 0);
  let perMinute: number = c_costPerMinute(state);
  let rows: ui.View[] = [];
  if (minutes <= 0) {
    rows.push(ui.Text("caption", "Cost per minute appears once watch time is logged above."));
  } else {
    rows.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.NumberStat("accent", "Cost per minute", perMinute, "$", "", 1, "monthly bill ÷ minutes watched", "chart", 4),
      ui.NumberStat("default", "Minutes watched", minutes, "", "", 1, "across all entries", "clock")
    ]));
    rows.push(ui.Text("caption", "$" + ui.formatNumber(monthlyCost, 2) + " monthly bill ÷ " + ui.formatNumber(minutes, 2) + " minutes"));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "Cost per minute", "", rows));
}

    picker.push(ui.Button("secondary", state.labels8[i], "c_pickRename", i, true));
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let renameRows: ui.View[] = [];
  renameRows.push(ui.Text("caption", "Tap a person, then type their name."));
  renameRows.push(ui.Row("default", picker));

Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.

- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. function c_totalMinutes(state: AppState): number {
  let sum: number = 0;
  for (let r: Tally of state.records8) {
    sum = sum + r.amount;
  }
  return math.round(sum * 100) / 100;
}

function c_costPerMinute(state: AppState): number {
  let monthlyCost: number = strings.toNumber(state.monthlyCostText, 0);
  let minutes: number = c_totalMinutes(state);
  if (minutes <= 0) { return 0; }
  return monthlyCost / minutes;
}

function c_setCurrency(state: AppState, index: number): AppState {
  let symbols: string[] = ["$", "€", "£", "¥", ""];
  let picked: string = "";
  if (index >= 0 && index < symbols.length()) { picked = symbols[index]; }
  return {currency8: picked__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>

{
  let minutes: number = c_totalMinutes(state);
  let monthlyCost: number = strings.toNumber(state.monthlyCostText, 0);
  let perMinute: number = c_costPerMinute(state);
  let symbols: string[] = ["$", "€", "£", "¥", "None"];
  let selected: number = 4;
  let s: number = 0;
  while (s < 4) {
    if (symbols[s] === state.currency8) { selected = s; }
    s = s + 1;
  }
  let rows: ui.View[] = [];
  rows.push(ui.Select("default", "Currency symbol", symbols, selected, "c_setCurrency"));
  if (minutes <= 0) {
    rows.push(ui.Text("caption", "Cost per minute appears once watch time is logged above."));
  } else {
    rows.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.NumberStat("accent", "Cost per minute", perMinute, state.currency8, "", 1, "monthly bill ÷ minutes watched", "chart", 4),
      ui.NumberStat("default", "Minutes watched", minutes, "", "", 1, "across all entries", "clock")
    ]));
    rows.push(ui.Text("caption", state.currency8 + ui.formatNumber(monthlyCost, 2) + " monthly bill ÷ " + ui.formatNumber(minutes, 2) + " minutes"));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "Cost per minute", "", rows));
}
</view>

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:

function c_shareOf(state: AppState, index: number): number {
  let totalBill: number = strings.toNumber(state.totalBillText, 0);
  let totalArea: number = strings.toNumber(state.totalAreaText, 0);
  let entryCount: number = state.entries.length();
  let entryTotal: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { entryTotal = entryTotal + e.squareFeet; }
  let ratePerSqFt: number = share(totalBill, totalArea);
  let sharedCost: number = share((totalBill - (ratePerSqFt * entryTotal)), entryCount);

}

        ui.formatNumber(c_e.squareFeet, 0) + " sq ft", c_amount, "$", "", 1, "", 0, false, ""));
      c_i = c_i + 1;
    }
    sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [
      ui.SectionHeader("default", "Each unit's share", "Square feet × rate + even share of common areas", ""),
      ui.Text("metric", "$" + c_rateText + " per sq ft"),
      ui.ListGroup("default", "", c_rows)
    ]));
  }
}

function c_shareOf(state: AppState, index: number): number {
  let totalBill: number = strings.toNumber(state.totalBillText, 0);
  let totalArea: number = strings.toNumber(state.totalAreaText, 0);

import * as ui from "std/ui"

@jsonable
class LogEntry {
  medicineName: string;
  doseGiven: number;
  minute: number;
}

@jsonable
class AppState {
  minGapHours: number;
  entries: LogEntry[];
  draft_medicineName: string;
  draft_doseGiven: string;
  removedEntries: LogEntry[];
  removedAt: number;
  settingsOpen: boolean;
}

function init(): AppState {
  let emptyEntries: LogEntry[] = [];
  return {minGapHours: 4, entries: emptyEntries, draft_medicineName: "", draft_doseGiven: "", removedEntries: emptyEntries, removedAt: -1, settingsOpen: false};
}

function share(a: number, b: number): number {
  if (b === 0) { return 0; }
  return a / b;
}



function set_minGapHours(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {minGapHours: value, entries: state.entries, draft_medicineName: state.draft_medicineName, draft_doseGiven: state.draft_doseGiven, removedEntries: state.removedEntries, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}



function set_draft_medicineName(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {draft_medicineName: value, minGapHours: state.minGapHours, entries: state.entries, draft_doseGiven: state.draft_doseGiven, removedEntries: state.removedEntries, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function set_draft_doseGiven(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {draft_doseGiven: value, minGapHours: state.minGapHours, entries: state.entries, draft_medicineName: state.draft_medicineName, removedEntries: state.removedEntries, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function addEntry(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (strings.trim(state.draft_medicineName) === "") { return state; }
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  let entry: LogEntry = {medicineName: strings.trim(state.draft_medicineName), doseGiven: strings.toNumber(state.draft_doseGiven, 0), minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()};
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { out.push(e); }
  out.push(entry);
  return {entries: out, removedEntries: none, draft_medicineName: "", draft_doseGiven: "", minGapHours: state.minGapHours, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function removeEntry(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  let gone: LogEntry[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    if (i !== value) { out.push(state.entries[i]); } else { gone.push(state.entries[i]); }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return {entries: out, removedEntries: gone, removedAt: value, minGapHours: state.minGapHours, draft_medicineName: state.draft_medicineName, draft_doseGiven: state.draft_doseGiven, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function undoRemove(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.removedEntries.length() === 0) { return state; }
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    if (i === state.removedAt) { out.push(state.removedEntries[0]); }
    out.push(state.entries[i]);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  if (state.removedAt >= state.entries.length()) { out.push(state.removedEntries[0]); }
  return {entries: out, removedEntries: none, removedAt: -1, minGapHours: state.minGapHours, draft_medicineName: state.draft_medicineName, draft_doseGiven: state.draft_doseGiven, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function expireUndo(state: AppState, elapsedMs: number): AppState {
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  return {removedEntries: none, removedAt: -1, minGapHours: state.minGapHours, entries: state.entries, draft_medicineName: state.draft_medicineName, draft_doseGiven: state.draft_doseGiven, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}





function toggleSettings(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {

function c_lastMinute(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = state.entries.length();
  if (n === 0) { return 0; }
  let best: number = state.entries[0].minute;
  let i: number = 1;
  while (i < n) {
    if (state.entries[i].minute > best) { best = state.entries[i].minute; }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return best;
}

function c_elapsedSeconds(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = state.entries.length();
  if (n === 0) { return 0; }
  let last: number = c_lastMinute(state);
  let nowMinute: number = time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour();
  let diff: number = nowMinute - last;
  if (diff < 0) { diff = diff + 1440; }
  return diff * 60;
}

function c_parseDate(s: string): number {
  let t: string = strings.trim(s);
  if (strings.length(t) === 0) { return -1; }
  let digits: string = "";
  for (let ch: string of t) {
    if (ch >= "0" && ch <= "9") { digits = digits + ch; }
  }
  if (strings.length(digits) !== 8) { return -1; }
  let y: number = strings.toNumber(strings.substring(digits, 0, 4), -1);
  let m: number = strings.toNumber(strings.substring(digits, 4, 6), -1);
  let d: number = strings.toNumber(strings.substring(digits, 6, 8), -1);
  if (y < 1 || m < 1 || m > 12 || d < 1 || d > 31) { return -1; }
  return y * 10000 + m * 100 + d;
}

function c_daysBetween(a: number, b: number): number {
  let diff: number = b - a;
  if (diff < 0) { diff = -diff; }
  return math.round(diff / 10000 * 365.25);
}

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

Request: savings pots for vacation and gifts

The section must do:
- the figure "Vacation saved": Total deposited into the vacation pot (money: show it with its currency sign $) (the plan works it out as entryTotal; for entryTotal = 350 that is 350)
- the figure "Gifts saved": Total deposited into the gifts pot (money: show it with its currency sign $) (the plan works it out as entryTotal; for entryTotal = 150 that is 150)
- the figure "Vacation progress": Share of the vacation goal saved so far (the plan works it out as vacationSaved / vacationGoal; for vacationSaved = 350, vacationGoal = 2000 that is 0.175)
- the figure "Gifts progress": Share of the gifts goal saved so far (the plan works it out as giftsSaved / giftsGoal; for giftsSaved = 150, giftsGoal = 500 that is 0.3)

The person sets these on the screen and nothing else uses them yet; the section uses them:
- "Vacation goal": state.vacationGoalText (the number as typed; strings.toNumber reads it)
- "Gifts goal": state.giftsGoalText (the number as typed; strings.toNumber reads it)

import * as ui from "std/ui"
import * as strings from "std/strings"

@jsonable
class Tally {
  who: number;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}

@jsonable
class AppState {
  vacationGoalText: string;
  giftsGoalText: string;
  labels7: string[];
  records7: Tally[];
  draftWho7: number;
  draftAmount7: string;
  draftNote7: string;
  currency7: string;
  settingsOpen: boolean;
}

function init(): AppState {
  let labels7: string[] = ["Vacation", "Gifts"];
  let records7: Tally[] = [];
  let currency7: string = "$";
  return {vacationGoalText: "2000", giftsGoalText: "500", labels7: labels7, records7: records7, draftWho7: 0, draftAmount7: "", draftNote7: "", currency7: currency7, settingsOpen: false};
}

function share(a: number, b: number): number {
  if (b === 0) { return 0; }
  return a / b;
}



function set_vacationGoal(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {vacationGoalText: value, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, labels7: state.labels7, records7: state.records7, draftWho7: state.draftWho7, draftAmount7: state.draftAmount7, draftNote7: state.draftNote7, currency7: state.currency7, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function set_giftsGoal(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {giftsGoalText: value, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, labels7: state.labels7, records7: state.records7, draftWho7: state.draftWho7, draftAmount7: state.draftAmount7, draftNote7: state.draftNote7, currency7: state.currency7, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}







function setWho7(state: AppState, index: number): AppState {
  return {labels7: state.labels7, records7: state.records7, draftWho7: index, draftAmount7: state.draftAmount7, draftNote7: state.draftNote7, currency7: state.currency7, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function setAmount7(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {labels7: state.labels7, records7: state.records7, draftWho7: state.draftWho7, draftAmount7: value, draftNote7: state.draftNote7, currency7: state.currency7, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function setNote7(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {labels7: state.labels7, records7: state.records7, draftWho7: state.draftWho7, draftAmount7: state.draftAmount7, draftNote7: value, currency7: state.currency7, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function addRecord7(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let amount: number = math.round(strings.toNumber(state.draftAmount7, 0) * 100) / 100;
  if (amount <= 0) { return state; }
  let out: Tally[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.records7.length()) {
    out.push(state.records7[i]);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  out.push({who: state.draftWho7, amount: amount, note: state.draftNote7});
  return {labels7: state.labels7, records7: out, draftWho7: state.draftWho7, draftAmount7: "", draftNote7: "", currency7: state.currency7, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function removeLastRecord7(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let out: Tally[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.records7.length() - 1) {
    out.push(state.records7[i]);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return {labels7: state.labels7, records7: out, draftWho7: state.draftWho7, draftAmount7: state.draftAmount7, draftNote7: state.draftNote7, currency7: state.currency7, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function clearRecords7(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let out: Tally[] = [];
  return {labels7: state.labels7, records7: out, draftWho7: 0, draftAmount7: "", draftNote7: "", currency7: state.currency7, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function totals7(state: AppState): number[] {
  let out: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.labels7.length()) {
    out.push(0);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  for (let r: Tally of state.records7) {
    if (r.who >= 0 && r.who < out.length()) { out[r.who] = math.round((out[r.who] + r.amount) * 100) / 100; }
  }
  return out;
}

function totalSum7(state: AppState): number {
  let sum: number = 0;
  for (let r: Tally of state.records7) { sum = sum + r.amount; }
  return math.round(sum * 100) / 100;
}

function average7(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = state.labels7.length();
  if (n === 0) { return 0; }
  return math.round(totalSum7(state) / n * 100) / 100;
}

function balances7(state: AppState): number[] {
  let totals: number[] = totals7(state);
  let n: number = state.labels7.length();
  let totalCents: number = math.round(totalSum7(state) * 100);
  let shareCents: number = 0;
  let extra: number = 0;
  if (n > 0) {
    shareCents = math.floor(totalCents / n);
    extra = totalCents - shareCents * n;
  }
  let out: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < totals.length()) {
    let owed: number = shareCents;
    if (i < extra) { owed = owed + 1; }
    out.push((math.round(totals[i] * 100) - owed) / 100);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return out;
}

function toggleSettings(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {settingsOpen: !state.settingsOpen, vacationGoalText: state.vacationGoalText, giftsGoalText: state.giftsGoalText, labels7: state.labels7, records7: state.records7, draftWho7: state.draftWho7, draftAmount7: state.draftAmount7, draftNote7: state.draftNote7, currency7: state.currency7};
}

function view(state: AppState): ui.View {
  let sections: ui.View[] = [];
  sections.push(ui.Header("default", "Savings Pots", "SAVINGS", "Track vacation and gift savings side by side", ""));
  {
      let vacationGoal: number = strings.toNumber(state.vacationGoalText, 0);
      let giftsGoal: number = strings.toNumber(state.giftsGoalText, 0);
  }
  {
      let n: number = state.records7.length();
      let plain: boolean = state.labels7.length() <= 1;
      let rows: ui.View[] = [];
      let k: number = n - 1;
      while (k >= 0) {
        let r: Tally = state.records7[k];
        let who: string = "?";
        if (r.who >= 0 && r.who < state.labels7.length()) { who = state.labels7[r.who]; }
        let shown: string = state.currency7 + ui.formatNumber(r.amount, 2);
        if (state.currency7.length() === 0) { shown = ui.numberToString(r.amount); }
        if (plain) {
          let title: string = r.note;
          if (title.length() === 0) { title = "Entry"; }
          rows.push(ui.ListItem("default", title, "", shown, "", k, false, ""));
        } else {
          rows.push(ui.ListItem("default", who, r.note, shown, "", k, false, ""));
        }
        k = k - 1;
      }
      let typed: number = strings.toNumber(state.draftAmount7, 0);
      if (plain) {
        let sumText: string = state.currency7 + ui.formatNumber(totalSum7(state), 2);
        if (state.currency7.length() === 0) { sumText = ui.numberToString(totalSum7(state)); }
        let avgText: string = "-";
        if (n > 0) {
          avgText = state.currency7 + ui.formatNumber(totalSum7(state) / n, 2);
          if (state.currency7.length() === 0) { avgText = ui.formatNumber(totalSum7(state) / n, 2); }
        }
        sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "", "", [
          ui.TileGrid("default", [
            ui.Tile("accent", 2, "Total", sumText, "all entries", "chart"),
            ui.Tile("default", 1, "Entries", ui.numberToString(n), "logged", "list"),
            ui.Tile("default", 1, "Average", avgText, "per entry", "chart")
          ])
        ]));
      }
      let compact7: boolean = false;
      let formRows: ui.View[] = [];
      if (!plain) { formRows.push(ui.Select("default", "Pot", state.labels7, state.draftWho7, "setWho7")); }
      formRows.push(ui.TextField("default", "Amount", state.draftAmount7, "setAmount7", "number"));
      sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Add Savings Pot", "", [
        ui.Column("default", formRows),
        ui.When(!compact7, ui.TextField("default", "Note", state.draftNote7, "setNote7")),
        ui.ActionBar("end", [
          ui.When(!compact7, ui.Button("danger", "Start over", "clearRecords7", 0, n > 0)),
          ui.Button("secondary", "Remove last", "removeLastRecord7", 0, n > 0),
          ui.Button("primary", "Add", "addRecord7", 0, typed > 0)
        ])
      ]));
      sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [
        ui.When(n === 0, ui.EmptyState("default", "Nothing yet", "Add the first record above.", "", "", "list")),
        ui.When(n > 0, ui.ListGroup("default", "", rows))
      ]));
    }
  {
    let settingsWord: string = "Show";
    if (state.settingsOpen) { settingsWord = "Hide"; }
    sections.push(ui.Section("supporting", "", "", [
      ui.ListItem("default", "Settings", "2 settings", settingsWord, "toggleSettings", 0, true, ""),
      ui.When(state.settingsOpen, ui.Column("default", [ui.TextField("default", "Vacation goal ($)", state.vacationGoalText, "set_vacationGoal", "number"), ui.TextField("default", "Gifts goal ($)", state.giftsGoalText, "set_giftsGoal", "number")]))
    ]));
  }
  return ui.AppTheme("clean", "", sections);
}

    ui.Stat("accent", "Vacation saved", c_vsText, "of " + c_vGoalText + " goal", "star"),
    ui.Stat("default", "Gifts saved", c_gsText, "of " + c_gGoalText + " goal", "star")
  ]));
  c_body.push(ui.Progress("accent", "Vacation progress " + c_vpText, c_vs, c_vg));
  c_body.push(ui.Progress("default", "Gifts progress " + c_gpText, c_gs, c_gg));

    c_body.push(ui.Text("caption", "Pot totals and progress appear here once you add savings above."));
  }

}

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

Request: money jars for weekly spending limits

The section must do:
- the figure "Spent this week": all the spending recorded so far added up (money: show it with its currency sign $) (the plan works it out as entryTotal; for entryTotal = 85 that is 85)
- the figure "Left this week": the weekly budget minus everything spent (money: show it with its currency sign $) (the plan works it out as weeklyBudget - spentTotal; for weeklyBudget = 200, spentTotal = 85 that is 115)
- the figure "Budget left": how much of the weekly budget is still unspent, as a fraction (the plan works it out as leftTotal / weeklyBudget; for leftTotal = 115, weeklyBudget = 200 that is 0.575)

The person sets these on the screen and nothing else uses them yet; the section uses them:
- "Weekly budget": state.weeklyBudgetText (the number as typed; strings.toNumber reads it)

The program already has these: use them, do not make your own:
- a list of entries: state.entries is LogEntry[] with the fields {jar: number, amount: number, noteItem: string, minute: number}. Its form, its Add and Remove buttons and its rows are already on the screen. The section makes no list of its own for the same entries; to add one it copies state.entries into a new array, pushes a LogEntry (minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()) and returns {entries: thatArray __PASSTHROUGH__}.

Nothing they show is shown again: no second list, total, chart, Remove last or Start over button. While what the section works from is still empty, it shows one plain line saying what will appear and when, never a ui.EmptyState: the list above already has one (two empty states one under the other read as a broken screen).

  return a / b;
}

}

  if (strings.trim(state.draft_noteItem) === "") { return state; }
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  let entry: LogEntry = {jar: strings.toNumber(state.draft_jar, 0), amount: strings.toNumber(state.draft_amount, 0), noteItem: strings.trim(state.draft_noteItem), minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()};
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { out.push(e); }
  out.push(entry);
  return {entries: out, removedEntries: none, draft_jar: "", draft_amount: "", draft_noteItem: "", weeklyBudgetText: state.weeklyBudgetText, jarCount: state.jarCount, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};

function removeEntry(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {

<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing

Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. function c_smallBlind(state: AppState): number {
  let roundLengthValues: number[] = [60, 120, 180, 300];
  let roundLength: number = roundLengthValues[state.roundLengthIndex];
  let duration: number = countdownSeconds(state);

<classes>
</classes>
<fields>
c_budget: string = ""
c_budgetSet: boolean = false
</fields>
<functions>
function c_setBudget(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_budget: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_applyBudget(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let typed: number = strings.toNumber(state.c_budget, 0);
  if (typed <= 0) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  return {c_budgetSet: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_clearBudget(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_budget: "", c_budgetSet: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_spent(state: AppState): number {
  let sum: number = 0;
  for (let r: Tally of state.records7) { sum = sum + r.amount; }
  return math.round(sum * 100) / 100;
}

function c_budgetValue(state: AppState): number {
  return math.round(strings.toNumber(state.c_budget, 0) * 100) / 100;
}

function c_remaining(state: AppState): number {
  return math.round((c_budgetValue(state) - c_spent(state)) * 100) / 100;
}

function c_money(state: AppState, amount: number): string {
  if (state.currency7.length() === 0) { return ui.formatNumber(amount, 2); }
  return state.currency7 + ui.formatNumber(amount, 2);
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let hasBudget: boolean = state.c_budgetSet && c_budgetValue(state) > 0;
  let spent: number = c_spent(state);
  let remaining: number = c_remaining(state);
  let over: boolean = remaining < 0;
  let budgetRows: ui.View[] = [];
  budgetRows.push(ui.TextField("default", "Total gift budget", state.c_budget, "c_setBudget", "number"));
  budgetRows.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [
    ui.When(hasBudget, ui.Button("secondary", "Change budget", "c_clearBudget", 0, true)),
    ui.Button("primary", "Set budget", "c_applyBudget", 0, strings.toNumber(state.c_budget, 0) > 0)
  ]));
  if (!hasBudget) {
    budgetRows.push(ui.Text("caption", "Set a total budget to see what is left after gifts."));
  } else {
    let tone: string = "success";
    if (over) { tone = "danger"; }
    let support: string = "of " + c_money(state, c_budgetValue(state)) + " budget";
    if (over) { support = "over the " + c_money(state, c_budgetValue(state)) + " budget"; }
    budgetRows.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 2, [
      ui.Stat(tone, "Remaining", c_money(state, remaining), support, "chart"),
      ui.Stat("default", "Spent", c_money(state, spent), "on gifts so far", "list")
    ]));
    if (state.records7.length() === 0) {
      budgetRows.push(ui.Text("caption", "Remaining will update as gifts are added above."));
    }
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "Remaining", "", budgetRows));
}
</view>

function c_dayCount(monthStart: number): number {
  let m: number = monthStart % 12;
  if (m < 0) { m = m + 12; }
  if (m === 1) { return 28; }
  if (m === 3 || m === 5 || m === 8 || m === 10) { return 30; }
  return 31;
}

function c_isRead(state: AppState, day: number): boolean {
  for (let d: number of state.c_readDays) {
    if (d === day) { return true; }
  }
  return false;
}

function c_toggleDay(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  let out: number[] = [];
  let found: boolean = false;
  for (let d: number of state.c_readDays) {
    if (d === value) {
      found = true;
    } else {
      out.push(d);
    }
  }
  if (!found) {
    out.push(value);
  }
  return {c_readDays: out__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_streak(state: AppState): number {
  let today: number = time.dayOfMonth();
  let count: number = 0;
  let d: number = today;
  let going: boolean = true;
  while (going && d >= 1) {
    if (c_isRead(state, d)) {
      count = count + 1;
      d = d - 1;
    } else {
      going = false;
    }
  }
  return count;
}

needs: A built-in quiz bank of common German nouns, each with its correct definite article (der, die, das) and an English meaning. The app picks questions from this bank for each round and shows the noun with three answer buttons: der, die, das. The person taps one; the app marks it right or wrong, shows the correct article, and moves to the next question until the chosen number of questions is done.
the figure "Correct": How many questions were answered correctly so far (the plan works it out as entryCount; for entryCount = 7 that is 7)

the figure "Accuracy": Share of answered questions that were correct (a percent: show it with the % sign) (the plan works it out as correctAnswers / entryCount * 100; for correctAnswers = 7, entryCount = 10 that is 70)

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion.     function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {

The section must do:
- A bank of decimal addition problems for each level: tenths (e.g. 0.3 + 0.4), hundredths (e.g. 0.25 + 0.13), mixed (e.g. 1.2 + 0.35), thousandths (e.g. 0.125 + 0.043) and challenge (e.g. 12.75 + 3.468). Nothing they show is shown again: no second list, total, chart, Remove last or Start over button. import * as ui from "std/ui"

@jsonable
class LogEntry {
  problem: string;
  answer: number;
  minute: number;
}

@jsonable
class AppState {
  levelIndex: number;
  questionsPerRound: number;
  entries: LogEntry[];
  draft_problem: string;
  draft_answer: string;
  removedEntries: LogEntry[];
  removedAt: number;
  settingsOpen: boolean;
}

function init(): AppState {
  let emptyEntries: LogEntry[] = [];
  return {levelIndex: 0, questionsPerRound: 10, entries: emptyEntries, draft_problem: "", draft_answer: "", removedEntries: emptyEntries, removedAt: -1, settingsOpen: false};
}

function share(a: number, b: number): number {
  if (b === 0) { return 0; }
  return a / b;
}



function set_level(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {levelIndex: value, questionsPerRound: state.questionsPerRound, entries: state.entries, draft_problem: state.draft_problem, draft_answer: state.draft_answer, removedEntries: state.removedEntries, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function set_questionsPerRound(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  return {questionsPerRound: value, levelIndex: state.levelIndex, entries: state.entries, draft_problem: state.draft_problem, draft_answer: state.draft_answer, removedEntries: state.removedEntries, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}



function set_draft_problem(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {draft_problem: value, levelIndex: state.levelIndex, questionsPerRound: state.questionsPerRound, entries: state.entries, draft_answer: state.draft_answer, removedEntries: state.removedEntries, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function set_draft_answer(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {draft_answer: value, levelIndex: state.levelIndex, questionsPerRound: state.questionsPerRound, entries: state.entries, draft_problem: state.draft_problem, removedEntries: state.removedEntries, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function addEntry(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (strings.trim(state.draft_problem) === "") { return state; }
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  let entry: LogEntry = {problem: strings.trim(state.draft_problem), answer: strings.toNumber(state.draft_answer, 0), minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()};
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { out.push(e); }
  out.push(entry);
  return {entries: out, removedEntries: none, draft_problem: "", draft_answer: "", levelIndex: state.levelIndex, questionsPerRound: state.questionsPerRound, removedAt: state.removedAt, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function removeEntry(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  let gone: LogEntry[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    if (i !== value) { out.push(state.entries[i]); } else { gone.push(state.entries[i]); }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return {entries: out, removedEntries: gone, removedAt: value, levelIndex: state.levelIndex, questionsPerRound: state.questionsPerRound, draft_problem: state.draft_problem, draft_answer: state.draft_answer, settingsOpen: state.settingsOpen};
}

function undoRemove(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.removedEntries.length() === 0) { return state; }
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    if (i === state.removedAt) { out.push(state.removedEntries[0]); }
    out.push(state.entries[i]);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  if (state.removedAt >= state.entries.length()) { out.push(state.removedEntries[0]); }
